title: Sets, real numbers and limits
goal: Fix the language of proof, state the axioms of the real numbers, and build limits, continuity and the mean value theorem, which every later analytic argument cites.

title: What this book builds, and the three questions it is aimed at
establishes: The three questions Q1-Q3 are stated in ordinary words; none can be posed precisely until the formalism is built, and the session names the Parts that each one needs.

title: Sets, functions and the forms of proof
establishes: Statements built from 'and', 'or', 'not', 'implies', 'for all' and 'there exists' have fixed negations, direct proof, contraposition and contradiction are valid methods, and a function is a bijection iff it has an inverse.

title: Mathematical induction and finite sums
establishes: The principle of induction proves statements for all natural numbers, and with it the rules for manipulating finite sums and products, including the binomial theorem and Bernoulli's inequality (1 + x)^n >= 1 + nx for every x >= -1 and every natural number n.

title: The real numbers and the least-upper-bound property
establishes: The real numbers form an ordered field in which every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound, and this property implies the Archimedean property.
gap: Omitted: the construction of R from Q (by Dedekind cuts or Cauchy sequences) and the proof that it satisfies the axioms. Why: it is long, and nothing later depends on the construction, only on the axioms. Where: W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 1 appendix.

title: Limits of real sequences
establishes: The absolute value satisfies the triangle inequality; a real sequence has at most one limit, convergent sequences are bounded, limits respect sums, products, quotients and non-strict inequalities, the squeeze rule holds, and r^n -> 0 when |r| < 1.

title: Monotone sequences, subsequences and Cauchy sequences
establishes: Every bounded monotone real sequence converges, every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence (Bolzano-Weierstrass), and a real sequence converges iff it is Cauchy.

title: Continuous functions on an interval
establishes: A real function on an interval is continuous at x iff f(x_n) -> f(x) for every sequence x_n -> x, and a continuous function on [a,b] is bounded, attains its maximum and minimum, and takes every value between f(a) and f(b); in particular every a >= 0 has a unique n-th root a^{1/n} >= 0, by the intermediate value theorem applied to x^n.

title: Limits of functions at a point
establishes: lim_{y->x} f(y) = L (epsilon-delta) holds iff f(y_n) -> L for every sequence y_n -> x with y_n != x, so limits of functions are unique and obey the sum, product and quotient rules, and f is continuous at x iff lim_{y->x} f(y) = f(x).

title: Derivatives and the mean value theorem
establishes: The derivative obeys the sum, product, quotient and chain rules, an interior extremum of a differentiable function has f' = 0, and Rolle's theorem and the mean value theorem follow, so f' = 0 on an interval forces f constant and f' >= 0 forces f nondecreasing.

title: Countable sets
establishes: A set is countable if it is empty or the range of a sequence; subsets and images of countable sets are countable, a countable union of sets each given with an enumeration is countable, and Q is countable; no interval of positive length is countable (nested intervals), so an interval minus a countable set is dense in it; and a monotone function on an interval is continuous except at countably many points, since each jump contains its own rational.

title: Problems for Part I
establishes: Integrated problems on induction, limits, continuity, countable sets and the mean value theorem, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Complex numbers, polynomials and groups
goal: Build the complex field, complex series and the exponential, Euler's formula and the number pi, polynomial roots and the first facts about groups.

title: The complex numbers as a field
establishes: Pairs of real numbers with (a,b)+(c,d) = (a+c,b+d) and (a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd,ad+bc) form a field C containing R, in which i^2 = -1.

title: Conjugation, modulus and the triangle inequality in C
establishes: Complex conjugation is a field automorphism with z conj(z) = |z|^2, the modulus is multiplicative, and |z+w| <= |z| + |w| with equality exactly when one is a nonnegative multiple of the other.

title: Sequences and series in C; absolute convergence
establishes: C is complete, a series converges iff its partial sums are Cauchy, an absolutely convergent series converges, and the comparison test and the ratio test (|a_{n+1}/a_n| <= r for some r < 1 and all large n) are sufficient conditions for absolute convergence.

title: Rearrangements and the Cauchy product
establishes: An absolutely convergent series may be rearranged without changing its sum, and the Cauchy product of two absolutely convergent series converges absolutely to the product of their sums.

title: The exponential series and its addition law
establishes: The series exp(z) = sum z^n/n! converges absolutely for every complex z, satisfies exp(z+w) = exp(z)exp(w), never vanishes, and obeys the tail bound |exp(z) - 1 - z| <= |z|^2 exp(|z|).

title: Derivatives of complex-valued functions of a real variable
establishes: Derivatives of functions R -> C, defined through real and imaginary parts, obey the sum and product rules, a function with zero derivative on an interval is constant, and d/dt exp(at) = a exp(at) for every complex a, by the tail bound of the exponential.

title: Euler's formula and the trigonometric functions
establishes: With cos t = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k t^{2k}/(2k)! and sin t = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k t^{2k+1}/(2k+1)!, both absolutely convergent for every real t, splitting the exponential series into its even and odd terms gives exp(it) = cos t + i sin t; then exp(it) exp(-it) = 1 gives cos^2 t + sin^2 t = 1, d/dt exp(it) = i exp(it) gives cos' = -sin and sin' = cos, and the addition formulas for cos and sin follow from exp(i(s+t)) = exp(is) exp(it).

title: The number pi and the periodicity of exp(it)
establishes: cos has a least positive zero, and pi is defined as twice it (cos 1 > 0 > cos 2 by the series, so 2 < pi < 4); then exp(i pi/2) = i, exp(it) = 1 exactly when t is an integer multiple of 2 pi, and t -> exp(it) maps [0, 2 pi) one-to-one onto the unit circle {z in C : |z| = 1}.

title: Polar form, phases and roots of unity
establishes: Every nonzero complex number is r exp(i theta) with r = |z| > 0 and theta unique in [0, 2 pi), multiplication multiplies moduli and adds phases, and with omega = exp(2 pi i/N) the N-th roots of unity omega^k (0 <= k < N) are the N distinct solutions of z^N = 1 and satisfy sum_{k=0}^{N-1} omega^{jk} = N if N divides j and 0 otherwise.

title: Complex polynomials: division and roots
establishes: A polynomial of degree n has at most n roots, and a is a root iff (z - a) divides it.

title: Continuous functions on a closed disc in C attain their minimum
establishes: A bounded sequence in C has a convergent subsequence (Bolzano-Weierstrass on real and imaginary parts), so a function f: C -> R with f(z_n) -> f(z) whenever z_n -> z attains its minimum on every closed disc |z| <= R, and |p| is such a function for every complex polynomial p.

title: Every nonconstant complex polynomial has a root
establishes: Since |p(z)| -> infinity as |z| -> infinity, |p| attains a global minimum at some z0; if p(z0) != 0, write p(z0+w)/p(z0) = 1 + a_k w^k + ... with a_k the lowest nonzero coefficient after the constant term, and a k-th root beta of -1/a_k gives |p(z0 + t beta)| < |p(z0)| for small t > 0; so every nonconstant complex polynomial has a root, and by induction p = c prod_i (z - a_i), uniquely up to the order of the factors.
note: Follow Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed., Ch. 4, result 4.12 (p. 125), or Rudin PMA Thm 8.8. a_k is the lowest nonzero coefficient of the expansion at z0, not the leading coefficient of p.

title: Groups, subgroups and homomorphisms
establishes: A group is a set with an associative operation, an identity and inverses, homomorphisms preserve the operation and have normal subgroups as kernels, and U(1) and Z_N are the first examples.

title: Permutations and the sign homomorphism
establishes: Every permutation is a product of transpositions, and the parity of the number of transpositions is well defined, giving a homomorphism sgn from S_n onto {+1,-1}.

title: Problems for Part II
establishes: Integrated problems on complex arithmetic, series, the exponential and permutations, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Vector spaces and linear maps
goal: Build abstract vector spaces over R and C, bases and dimension, linear maps and their matrices, the dual space, the determinant and the trace.

title: Vector spaces over C and over R
establishes: A vector space is a set with addition and scalar multiplication satisfying eight axioms, the zero vector and additive inverses are unique, and C^n, the 2x2 complex matrices, polynomials of bounded degree and complex functions on a finite set are examples.

title: Subspaces, sums of subspaces and spans
establishes: The span of a list is the smallest subspace containing it, and a sum of subspaces is direct exactly when the only way to write 0 is with all summands 0.

title: Linear independence
establishes: A list is linearly independent iff no vector in it lies in the span of the others, and in a linearly dependent list some vector lies in the span of the previous ones and can be removed without changing the span.

title: The exchange lemma
establishes: In a space spanned by m vectors, every linearly independent list has at most m vectors.

title: Bases and coordinates
establishes: Every spanning list of a finite-dimensional space contains a basis, every independent list extends to a basis, and coordinates with respect to a basis are unique.

title: Dimension
establishes: All bases of a finite-dimensional space have the same length, so dimension is well defined, and a list whose length is the dimension is a basis iff it is independent iff it spans.

title: The dimension of a sum of subspaces
establishes: dim(U+W) = dim U + dim W - dim(U intersect W), so a sum is direct iff the dimensions add, and every subspace has a complement.

title: Linear maps, kernel and image
establishes: A linear map is fixed by its values on a basis, its kernel and image are subspaces, and it is injective iff its kernel is zero.

title: The rank-nullity theorem
establishes: For a linear map T on a finite-dimensional space V, dim V = dim ker T + dim im T, so an operator on V is injective iff it is surjective.

title: The matrix of a linear map; composition is matrix multiplication
establishes: Fixing bases turns linear maps into matrices so that composition of maps becomes the matrix product and evaluation becomes matrix-vector multiplication.

title: Invertible maps and isomorphisms
establishes: A linear map is invertible iff it is bijective, its inverse is linear, a one-sided inverse of an operator is two-sided, and two finite-dimensional spaces over the same field are isomorphic iff they have the same dimension.

title: Change of basis and similarity
establishes: The matrices of one operator in two bases are related by A' = S^{-1} A S with S the change-of-basis matrix, so similarity-invariant quantities are properties of the operator.

title: The space of linear maps and the dual space
establishes: L(V,W) is a vector space of dimension (dim V)(dim W), and the dual space V* = L(V,F), with F = R or C the scalar field, has a dual basis with as many elements as a basis of V.

title: Alternating multilinear forms are determined by one number
establishes: A function of n columns that is multilinear and alternating changes sign when two columns are swapped, vanishes on linearly dependent columns, and equals its value on the identity times the Leibniz sum of signed products over permutations.

title: The determinant exists and equals that of the transpose
establishes: The Leibniz sum is multilinear, alternating and equal to 1 on the identity, so the determinant exists and is unique, and det(A^T) = det A.

title: The determinant of a product and the invertibility criterion
establishes: det(AB) = det A det B, A is invertible iff det A is nonzero, and the determinant of an operator does not depend on the basis.

title: The trace of a matrix and of an operator
establishes: The trace is linear and satisfies tr(AB) = tr(BA) for rectangular A and B of compatible shapes, so it is a similarity invariant and a property of the operator.

title: The Pauli matrices: with I, a basis for 2x2 matrices, and their product rule
establishes: I, sigma_x, sigma_y, sigma_z form a basis of the 2x2 complex matrices with sigma_j sigma_k = delta_jk I + i epsilon_jkl sigma_l, so each Pauli matrix is traceless with determinant -1 and square I.

title: Problems for Part III
establishes: Integrated problems on bases, matrices, determinants and the Pauli matrices, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Inner-product spaces
goal: Add lengths and angles: inner products, Cauchy-Schwarz, orthonormal bases, projections, Dirac notation, adjoints, and the special classes of operators the postulates use.

title: Inner products over R and over C
establishes: A complex inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, linear in the second, conjugate-symmetric and positive definite, a real inner product is the same with real scalars and symmetry, and sum_i conj(x_i) y_i on C^n and sum_i x_i y_i on R^n are examples.

title: Norm, orthogonality and the Pythagorean theorem
establishes: ||v|| = sqrt<v,v> is positive and homogeneous, and orthogonal vectors satisfy ||u+v||^2 = ||u||^2 + ||v||^2.

title: The Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities
establishes: |<u,v>| <= ||u|| ||v|| with equality iff u and v are linearly dependent, and hence ||u+v|| <= ||u|| + ||v||.

title: The polarisation identity
establishes: The inner product is determined by the norm through the polarisation identities over R and over C, and over C an operator T with <v,Tv> = 0 for every v is zero.

title: Orthonormal lists and expansion in an orthonormal basis
establishes: An orthonormal list is independent, and in an orthonormal basis v = sum_i <e_i,v> e_i with ||v||^2 = sum_i |<e_i,v>|^2.

title: The Gram-Schmidt procedure
establishes: Every independent list can be replaced by an orthonormal list with the same successive spans, so every finite-dimensional inner-product space has an orthonormal basis and every orthonormal list extends to one.

title: Orthogonal complements and orthogonal decomposition
establishes: For a subspace U, V = U (+) U^perp as a direct sum, dim U^perp = dim V - dim U, and (U^perp)^perp = U.

title: Orthogonal projection onto a subspace and best approximation
establishes: The orthogonal projection P_U v = sum <e_i,v> e_i over an orthonormal basis of U is the unique point of U closest to v, and v - P_U v lies in U^perp.

title: The Riesz representation theorem
establishes: Every linear functional f on a finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product space is f(v) = <u,v> for exactly one vector u, giving a bijection (conjugate-linear over C) between V and V*.

title: Dirac notation: kets, bras and outer products
establishes: Writing |v> for v and <u| for the functional <u,.>, the outer product |u><v| is the operator w -> <v,w> u, and sum_i |e_i><e_i| = I for every orthonormal basis, and tr(A|u><v|) = <v|A|u>, so <psi|A|psi> = tr(A |psi><psi|).

title: The adjoint of a linear map
establishes: Every linear map T has a unique adjoint T^dagger with <u,Tv> = <T^dagger u,v>, its matrix in orthonormal bases is the conjugate transpose, (ST)^dagger = T^dagger S^dagger, and ker T^dagger = (im T)^perp.

title: Self-adjoint operators
establishes: On a complex inner-product space T is self-adjoint iff <v,Tv> is real for every v, and the self-adjoint operators form a real vector space of real dimension n^2, with I and the Pauli matrices as a basis when n = 2.

title: Orthogonal projectors as self-adjoint idempotents
establishes: An operator is an orthogonal projection onto a subspace iff P^2 = P = P^dagger, and a sum of projectors is a projector iff they are pairwise orthogonal, P_i P_j = 0, in which case it projects onto the direct sum of their images.

title: Isometries and unitary operators
establishes: A linear map V satisfies V^dagger V = I iff it preserves inner products iff it maps orthonormal lists to orthonormal lists, an operator with this property is unitary (U^dagger = U^{-1}) and the unitaries form the group U(n), and an isometry from a subspace U of W into W extends to a unitary on W.

title: Normal operators
establishes: T is normal (T T^dagger = T^dagger T) iff ||Tv|| = ||T^dagger v|| for all v, and then T and T^dagger have the same kernel.

title: The Hilbert-Schmidt inner product on operators
establishes: <A,B> = tr(A^dagger B) is an inner product on L(V), I/sqrt2, sigma_x/sqrt2, sigma_y/sqrt2, sigma_z/sqrt2 form an orthonormal basis for n = 2, tr(AB) is a real inner product on the self-adjoint operators, and so every real-linear functional on them is X -> tr(HX) for exactly one self-adjoint H.

title: Problems for Part IV
establishes: Integrated problems on orthonormal bases, projectors, adjoints and the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product in C^2 and C^3, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Spectral theory
goal: Prove that normal operators have orthonormal eigenbases, in small steps from the existence of one eigenvalue, and build the functional calculus, commutators and rotations of R^3.

title: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and eigenspaces
establishes: lambda is an eigenvalue of T iff T - lambda I is not injective, and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent, so an operator on an n-dimensional space has at most n eigenvalues.

title: Polynomials applied to operators
establishes: p -> p(T) is a homomorphism from polynomials to operators, so p(T)q(T) = q(T)p(T), and a factorisation of p gives a factorisation of p(T).

title: Every operator on a nonzero complex space has an eigenvalue
establishes: Every operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space has an eigenvalue, proved by factoring a polynomial that annihilates a nonzero vector v, Tv, ..., T^n v.

title: Invariant subspaces and upper-triangular matrices
establishes: The matrix of T in a basis is upper triangular iff the span of the first k basis vectors is T-invariant for every k, every operator on a finite-dimensional complex space has such a basis, and the diagonal entries are then exactly its eigenvalues.

title: Schur's theorem
establishes: Every operator on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space is upper triangular in some orthonormal basis, by applying Gram-Schmidt to a triangularising basis.

title: The spectral theorem for normal operators
establishes: An operator on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors iff it is normal, proved by showing that a normal upper-triangular matrix is diagonal.

title: Spectra of self-adjoint, unitary and projection operators
establishes: A normal operator is self-adjoint iff its eigenvalues are real, unitary iff they have modulus 1, and an orthogonal projector iff they lie in {0,1}.

title: Spectral decomposition into eigenprojections
establishes: A normal T equals sum_k lambda_k P_k with distinct lambda_k and pairwise orthogonal projectors P_k summing to I, this decomposition is unique, and each P_k is a polynomial in T.

title: The characteristic polynomial
establishes: The eigenvalues of T are exactly the roots of det(zI - T), a basis-independent polynomial of degree n whose roots, counted with multiplicity, are the diagonal of any triangular form, so det T is their product and tr T their sum.

title: Commutators
establishes: The commutator [A,B] = AB - BA is bilinear and antisymmetric, obeys [A,BC] = [A,B]C + B[A,C] and the Jacobi identity, is anti-self-adjoint when A and B are self-adjoint, and [sigma_j, sigma_k] = 2i epsilon_jkl sigma_l.

title: Simultaneous diagonalisation of commuting normal operators
establishes: A family of normal operators has a common orthonormal eigenbasis iff its members commute pairwise, proved by restricting each operator to the eigenspaces of another.

title: Functions of a normal operator
establishes: For a normal T = sum lambda_k P_k and any function f on its spectrum, f(T) = sum f(lambda_k) P_k is well defined, agrees with p(T) for polynomials p, and satisfies (fg)(T) = f(T)g(T) and f(T)^dagger = conj(f)(T).

title: Real orthogonal matrices and the rotation group SO(3)
establishes: A real orthogonal 3x3 matrix has determinant +-1; one with determinant +1 fixes a unit vector m (non-real eigenvalues of a real matrix come in conjugate pairs) and, with (m x v)_l = epsilon_jkl m_j v_k, acts as Rv = (m.v)m + cos(theta)(v - (m.v)m) + sin(theta)(m x v) for some theta (Euler's rotation theorem); the rotations about a fixed axis form a subgroup isomorphic to U(1).

title: Problems for Part V
establishes: Integrated problems diagonalising 2x2 and 3x3 normal matrices and computing functions of them, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Finite probability
goal: Build probability on finite sample spaces: conditioning, independence, random variables, expectation, conditional expectation, the weak law and total variation.

title: Finite probability spaces and events
establishes: A probability on a finite set assigns nonnegative weights summing to 1, events are subsets, and P(complement of A) = 1 - P(A), monotonicity, the union bound and P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersect B) hold.

title: Conditional probability, total probability and Bayes' rule
establishes: P(A|B) = P(A intersect B)/P(B) defines a probability, the chain rule holds, P(A) = sum_i P(A|B_i)P(B_i) for a partition, and P(B_i|A) = P(A|B_i)P(B_i)/P(A).

title: Independence of events
establishes: Events are independent when their joint probabilities factor, pairwise independence does not imply mutual independence, and independence of A and B is equivalent to P(A|B) = P(A) when P(B) > 0.

title: Random variables, joint distributions and marginals
establishes: A random variable is a function on the sample space, a family of them has a joint distribution whose marginals are obtained by summing, and not every family of pairwise marginals arises from one joint distribution.

title: Independence and conditional independence of random variables
establishes: X and Y are conditionally independent given Z iff p(x,y|z) = p(x|z)p(y|z), and this neither implies nor is implied by unconditional independence.

title: Product probability spaces and independent copies
establishes: For finite probability spaces (Omega_i, p_i), the weights p_1(w_1)...p_n(w_n) on Omega_1 x ... x Omega_n form a probability space on which the coordinates are mutually independent with marginals p_i, so n independent copies of any random variable exist.

title: Expectation and its linearity
establishes: E[X] = sum_x x p(x) is linear and monotone, multiplicative for independent random variables, with E[prod f_i(X_i)] = prod E[f_i(X_i)] for mutually independent X_1, ..., X_n, and E[X|B] satisfies E[X] = sum_i E[X|B_i] P(B_i) for a partition.

title: Variance, covariance and correlation
establishes: Var(X) = E[X^2] - E[X]^2 >= 0 with equality iff X is constant with probability 1, variance is additive for independent variables, and |Cov(X,Y)| <= sqrt(Var X Var Y) by Cauchy-Schwarz for <X,Y> = E[XY], an inner product on real functions on the support {p > 0}.

title: Conditional expectation, the tower property and martingales
establishes: E[X|Y] is the random variable taking the value E[X|Y=y] on {Y=y}, it satisfies E[E[X|Y]] = E[X] and E[g(Y)X|Y] = g(Y)E[X|Y], and a sequence with E[X_{n+1}|X_1,...,X_n] = X_n (a martingale) has constant expectation.

title: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities; the weak law of large numbers
establishes: P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a for X >= 0, P(|X - E X| >= a) <= Var X/a^2, and the mean of n independent copies lies within epsilon of the expectation with probability at least 1 - Var/(n epsilon^2).

title: Total variation distance and optimal guessing between two distributions
establishes: Given one sample from p or q with prior probabilities 1/2 each, the best guess is correct with probability (1 + TV(p,q))/2, where TV(p,q) = (1/2) sum |p(x) - q(x)| = max_A |p(A) - q(A)|, and |E_p f - E_q f| <= 2 TV(p,q) whenever |f| <= 1.

title: Problems for Part VI
establishes: Integrated problems on Bayes' rule, conditional expectation, Chebyshev bounds and total variation, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: The postulates for a single system
goal: State the postulates for states, observables, outcome probabilities and state update, and work them out on the qubit, on interferometers and on uncertainty relations.

title: Preparations, measurements and outcome probabilities
establishes: A physical theory of the kind studied here assigns to each preparation and each measurement a probability distribution over outcomes, and mixing preparations with weights p_i must mix these distributions with the same weights.

title: States, observables and the Born rule
establishes: Postulates: a system has a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, a pure state is a unit vector, an observable is a self-adjoint operator A = sum a_k P_k, and outcome a_k occurs with probability <psi|P_k|psi>, so the outcome distribution has mean <psi|A|psi> and variance <psi|A^2|psi> - <psi|A|psi>^2.

title: The state-update rule for projective measurements
establishes: Postulate: after outcome a_k the state becomes P_k psi/||P_k psi|| (the Luders rule), so an immediately repeated measurement gives a_k again, and outcomes a_k then b_l occur in sequence with probability ||Q_l P_k psi||^2.

title: Global phase is unobservable; relative phase is observable
establishes: Two unit vectors give the same probabilities for every measurement iff they differ by a factor exp(i theta), so states are rays, while (|0> + exp(i phi)|1>)/sqrt2 for different phi are distinguished by measuring in another basis.

title: Pure qubit states and the Bloch sphere
establishes: Rays in C^2 correspond bijectively to points n of the unit sphere via |psi><psi| = (I + n.sigma)/2, every qubit state is cos(theta/2)|0> + exp(i phi) sin(theta/2)|1> up to phase, and orthogonal rays correspond to antipodal points.

title: Spin observables along a direction
establishes: m.sigma has eigenvalues +1 and -1 with eigenprojectors (I +- m.sigma)/2, and in the state with Bloch vector n the outcome +1 has probability (1 + m.n)/2 and the mean is m.n.

title: Experiment: the Stern-Gerlach apparatus and idealised sequential measurements
establishes: The Stern-Gerlach apparatus (Stern and Gerlach 1922, silver atoms, a single magnet) is modelled as a measurement of m.sigma on a spin-1/2 system, and the idealised sequence z, then x, then z predicts 1/2 and 1/2 for the final z, as the state-update rule requires, contrary to any model in which the z and x values are both retained.

title: Photon polarisation as a qubit
establishes: Photon polarisation is a qubit in which a polariser at angle theta is the projector onto (cos theta, sin theta), giving Malus's law cos^2, and wave plates act as unitaries; polarisers at 0, 45 and 90 degrees pass 1/4 of the light leaving the first, where crossed polarisers pass none, a performed analogue of the z, x, z sequence; this is the qubit of most Bell experiments.

title: Beam splitters and the Mach-Zehnder interferometer
establishes: With the two paths of a photon as a qubit, a balanced beam splitter is a Hadamard-type unitary and a phase shifter is diag(1, exp(i phi)), so the output probabilities are (1 +- cos phi)/2 and the fringe visibility is 1.

title: Commutators and compatible observables
establishes: For projective measurements of A and B, the joint probabilities of sequential measurement are independent of the order for every state iff [A,B] = 0, and then a single measurement in a common eigenbasis yields both values.

title: The Robertson uncertainty relation
establishes: For every state psi and self-adjoint A and B, Delta A Delta B >= (1/2)|<psi|[A,B]|psi>|, proved by Cauchy-Schwarz on the vectors (A - <A>)psi and (B - <B>)psi, and the Schrodinger form adds the anticommutator term.

title: The Robertson relation for qubit spin components, and what it constrains
establishes: For sigma_x and sigma_y the relation reads Delta X Delta Y >= |n_z|, a bound on the spreads of two separate measurements on identically prepared systems, which says nothing about one measurement disturbing another.

title: Position and momentum on a ring of N sites
establishes: On C^N the shift X|j> = |j+1> and the clock Z|j> = omega^j |j> satisfy ZX = omega XZ, the discrete Fourier transform exchanges their eigenbases, and the two eigenbases are mutually unbiased.

title: No finite matrices satisfy [Q,P] = i hbar I
establishes: Taking the trace of both sides shows that no operators Q, P on a finite-dimensional space satisfy [Q,P] = cI for any c != 0, in particular the canonical relation with c = i hbar, where hbar is the reduced Planck constant, fixed here and used from the dynamics postulate on.

title: Excursion: wavefunctions on the line, position and momentum
establishes: Letting the ring's spacing go to zero leads to wavefunctions psi(x) with |psi|^2 a probability density, position as multiplication by x and momentum as -i hbar d/dx, which satisfy [x,p] = i hbar on smooth rapidly decaying functions, a relation only unbounded operators can satisfy.
gap: Omitted: L^2(R), unbounded self-adjoint operators and their domains, their spectral theorem, the Fourier transform on L^2, and the theorem that no bounded operators on a Hilbert space satisfy [x,p] = i hbar I (Wintner 1947, Wielandt 1949). Why: they need Lebesgue integration and infinite-dimensional functional analysis; the trace argument of no-canonical-pair-finite does not extend, since there is no trace on all bounded operators. Where: Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chs 3-4 and 9-10 and App. A; A. Wintner, Phys. Rev. 71 (1947) 738; H. Wielandt, Math. Ann. 121 (1949) 21.

title: Excursion: Heisenberg's position-momentum relation
establishes: Applying the Robertson argument formally to x and p gives Kennard's inequality Delta x Delta p >= hbar/2 (Kennard 1927, the sharp form of Heisenberg's 1927 heuristic relation), with equality exactly for psi(x) = c exp(-(x-x0)^2/(4 s^2) + i p0 x/hbar) with real s > 0.
gap: Omitted: the justification of the Robertson argument for unbounded operators (the state must lie in the domains of xp and px) and the Gaussian integrals. Why: domains of unbounded operators are outside the book. Where: Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Ch. 12 (12.1 and 12.3 the statements and proof, 12.2 the domain counterexample, 12.4 minimum-uncertainty states).

title: Problems for Part VII
establishes: Integrated problems on qubit measurement sequences, interferometers and uncertainty relations, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Integrals, Taylor's theorem and the analysis of operators
goal: Build Taylor's theorem and the integral, then norms, series and integrals of operators, the matrix exponential, and the theorem that a continuous unitary group has a self-adjoint generator.

title: The real exponential and the logarithm
establishes: A continuous strictly increasing function on an interval has a continuous inverse, differentiable wherever f' != 0 with (f^{-1})'(y) = 1/f'(f^{-1}(y)); on R, exp is real, positive and strictly increasing with exp' = exp, and a bijection onto (0, infinity), so its inverse log is differentiable with log'(x) = 1/x, and log(xy) = log x + log y.

title: Taylor's theorem with the Lagrange remainder
establishes: If f is n+1 times differentiable on an interval containing a and x, then f(x) equals its degree-n Taylor polynomial at a plus f^(n+1)(c)(x-a)^(n+1)/(n+1)! for some c between a and x, which gives 1 - cos x <= x^2/2, exp(x) >= 1 + x and log(1+x) <= x.

title: Uniform continuity on a closed interval
establishes: A continuous function on [a,b] is uniformly continuous, proved by contradiction from the Bolzano-Weierstrass property.

title: The Riemann integral of a continuous function
establishes: Every continuous f on [a,b] has a Riemann integral (sup of lower sums = inf of upper sums), which is linear, monotone, additive over adjacent intervals, translation invariant (integral_a^b f(s+t) ds = integral_{a+t}^{b+t} f) and satisfies |integral f| <= integral |f|.

title: The fundamental theorem of calculus
establishes: For continuous f, F(x) = integral_a^x f has F' = f, so (1/eps) integral_t^{t+eps} f -> f(t), and integral_a^b g' = g(b) - g(a) for continuously differentiable g.

title: Convergence of vectors and matrices
establishes: A sequence in C^n converges in the standard norm, and a sequence of n x n matrices in the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, iff it converges entrywise, and both spaces are complete.

title: Derivatives and integrals of matrix-valued functions
establishes: Entrywise derivatives and integrals of continuous functions t -> A(t) obey the product rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus, ||integral A|| <= integral ||A|| for every norm that comes from an inner product, and integral C A(s) ds = C integral A(s) ds and integral A(s) C ds = (integral A(s) ds) C for every constant matrix C.

title: The operator norm
establishes: ||T|| = sup_{||v|| = 1} ||Tv|| is finite, a norm, submultiplicative, satisfies ||T^dagger|| = ||T|| and ||T^dagger T|| = ||T||^2, and equals the largest |eigenvalue| when T is normal.

title: Operator-norm convergence, completeness and integrals
establishes: |T_ij| <= ||T|| <= (sum_ij |T_ij|^2)^{1/2} in an orthonormal basis, so operator-norm convergence is entrywise convergence and L(C^n) is complete in the operator norm, and ||integral A(t) dt|| <= integral ||A(t)|| dt in the operator norm, by applying the vector inequality of matrix-valued-functions to A(t)v.

title: Operator series and the matrix exponential
establishes: A series of operators with summable operator norms converges, and the Cauchy product of two such series converges in norm to the product of their sums, by the argument of cauchy-product with |.| replaced by the operator norm; so exp(A) = sum A^n/n! exists for every operator, with ||exp(A)|| <= exp(||A||) and ||exp(A) - I - A|| <= ||A||^2 exp(||A||).

title: Properties of the matrix exponential
establishes: exp(A+B) = exp(A)exp(B) when AB = BA, exp(A) is invertible with inverse exp(-A), exp(SAS^{-1}) = S exp(A) S^{-1}, exp of a normal operator agrees with the functional calculus, and exp(iH) is unitary for self-adjoint H.

title: The derivative of exp(tA) and uniqueness for x' = Ax
establishes: d/dt exp(tA) = A exp(tA), and x(t) = exp(tA)x(0) is the unique differentiable solution of x' = Ax with the given initial value.

title: Exponentials of Pauli combinations
establishes: exp(-i (theta/2) n.sigma) = cos(theta/2) I - i sin(theta/2) n.sigma for every unit vector n, because (n.sigma)^2 = I.

title: The Lie-Trotter product formula
establishes: For all operators A and B, (exp(A/n) exp(B/n))^n converges to exp(A+B) as n -> infinity, with error O(1/n), via the telescoping bound ||X^n - Y^n|| <= n M^(n-1) ||X - Y|| for ||X||, ||Y|| <= M, so X_n^n -> exp(L) whenever ||X_n - exp(L/n)|| = O(1/n^2).

title: The Neumann series
establishes: If ||I - M|| < 1 then M is invertible with M^{-1} = sum_n (I - M)^n.

title: A continuous one-parameter group of operators is differentiable
establishes: If t -> U(t) is continuous with U(s+t) = U(s)U(t) and U(0) = I, then V = (1/eps) integral_0^eps U(s) ds is invertible for small eps and U(t) = V^{-1} (1/eps) integral_t^{t+eps} U(s) ds, so U is differentiable.

title: One-parameter unitary groups are exponentials
establishes: Every continuous map t -> U(t) into the unitaries with U(s+t) = U(s)U(t) and U(0) = I has the form U(t) = exp(-itH) for exactly one self-adjoint H, namely H = i U'(0).

title: Gronwall's inequality and uniqueness for time-dependent linear equations
establishes: If u >= 0 is differentiable on [0,T] with u' <= a(t)u for continuous a >= 0 and u(0) = 0, then u = 0 on [0,T]; applied to ||x - y||^2 forward and backward in time, x' = A(t)x with continuous A(t) has at most one solution on any interval through t0 with given x(t0).
gap: Omitted: existence of solutions of x' = A(t)x for general continuous A(t) (Picard-Lindelof). Why: the book needs existence only for piecewise-constant A(t) or for explicit solutions, where it is constructed directly; the general case needs uniform convergence of function sequences. Where: G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Thm 2.2 and Sec. 3.4.

title: Problems for Part VIII
establishes: Integrated problems on Taylor bounds, operator norms, exponentials of Pauli combinations and linear differential equations, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Dynamics of a closed system
goal: State the dynamics postulate, derive the Schrodinger equation from a continuous unitary group law, solve qubit dynamics, prove that SU(2) covers SO(3), and pass to the Heisenberg picture.

title: The dynamics postulate and the Schrodinger equation
establishes: Postulate: a closed system evolves by unitaries U(t) with U(s+t) = U(s)U(t) depending continuously on t; hence U(t) = exp(-iHt/hbar) for a unique self-adjoint Hamiltonian H, and psi(t) is the unique solution of i hbar d psi/dt = H psi.

title: Evolution under a constant Hamiltonian: energy eigenstates and phases
establishes: In the eigenbasis of H each energy eigenstate only acquires the phase exp(-i E_k t/hbar), so energy eigenstates have time-independent outcome distributions, only energy differences are observable, and every evolution is a superposition of these phases.

title: Larmor precession and Rabi oscillation for a static Hamiltonian
establishes: For H = (hbar/2)(Delta Z + Omega X) the probability of finding |1> after starting in |0> is Omega^2/(Omega^2 + Delta^2) sin^2(sqrt(Omega^2 + Delta^2) t/2), and for Omega = 0 the relative phase of |0> and |1> advances at angular frequency Delta.

title: SU(2) acts on Bloch vectors by orthogonal maps
establishes: For U in SU(2), U (n.sigma) U^dagger = (R_U n).sigma defines a real orthogonal 3x3 matrix R_U, and U -> R_U is a homomorphism, R_{UV} = R_U R_V.

title: SU(2) is a two-to-one cover of SO(3)
establishes: exp(-i theta m.sigma/2) maps to the rotation by theta about m, every element of SU(2) has this form by the spectral theorem, so U -> R_U maps SU(2) onto SO(3) with kernel {I, -I}, and a rotation by 2 pi acts on state vectors as -I.

title: Bloch-vector precession under a static spin Hamiltonian
establishes: Under H = (hbar omega/2) m.sigma the Bloch vector of every state rotates about m at angular frequency omega.

title: Time-dependent Hamiltonians
establishes: For piecewise-constant H(t), the unique continuous psi satisfying i hbar psi' = H(t) psi away from the switching times is the ordered product of exponentials; for continuous H(t) the Schrodinger equation has at most one solution, which preserves norms whenever it exists.
gap: Omitted: existence of the solution for general continuous H(t), and its expression as a time-ordered exponential. Why: the book needs only piecewise-constant Hamiltonians and explicitly solvable ones; see the gap in gronwall-uniqueness. Where: Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Sec. 3.4; M. Reed and B. Simon, Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics II, Sec. X.12.

title: Every qubit unitary from Z and X rotations
establishes: Every rotation of R^3 is R_z(a) R_x(b) R_z(c) for some angles (Euler angles, proved directly), so every qubit unitary is, up to a global phase, exp(-iaZ/2) exp(-ibX/2) exp(-icZ/2), and piecewise-constant Z and X Hamiltonians generate every qubit unitary.

title: A resonant drive and the rotating frame
establishes: For H(t) = (hbar/2)(omega_0 Z + Omega(cos(omega t) X + sin(omega t) Y)) the function exp(-i omega t Z/2) exp(-i H' t/hbar) psi_0, with H' = (hbar/2)((omega_0 - omega) Z + Omega X), solves the Schrodinger equation and is therefore its unique solution, so the static Rabi formula with detuning omega_0 - omega describes resonance.

title: The Heisenberg picture
establishes: Evolving observables by A(t) = U(t)^dagger A U(t) and keeping the state fixed gives the same probabilities, and A(t) satisfies dA/dt = (i/hbar)[H, A(t)].

title: Conserved observables
establishes: The outcome distribution of A is the same at all times for every initial state iff [H,A] = 0.

title: Problems for Part IX
establishes: Integrated problems on qubit dynamics in both pictures, Bloch rotations and control sequences, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Positivity, singular values and the trace norm
goal: Build positive operators and their square roots, the singular value and polar decompositions, the equal-Gram lemma, the trace norm and the Powers-Stormer inequality.

title: Positive operators
establishes: For an operator A on a complex inner-product space the following are equivalent: <v,Av> >= 0 for all v; A is self-adjoint with nonnegative eigenvalues; A = B^dagger B for some B.

title: The positive square root
establishes: Every positive operator A has exactly one positive operator R with R^2 = A, and R commutes with every operator that commutes with A.

title: The operator order and effects
establishes: A <= B iff B - A is positive defines a partial order preserved by A -> X^dagger A X, tr(AB) >= 0 for positive A and B, and the effects 0 <= E <= I are exactly the self-adjoint operators with spectrum in [0,1].

title: The singular value decomposition
establishes: Every linear map T: V -> W between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces is T = sum_k s_k |f_k><e_k| with s_k > 0 and orthonormal lists (e_k), (f_k), obtained from an orthonormal eigenbasis (e_k) of T^dagger T with eigenvalues s_k^2 and f_k = T e_k/s_k.

title: Uniqueness and meaning of singular values
establishes: The singular values of T are uniquely determined, their number is rank T, the largest is ||T||, and they are unchanged by T -> UTV for unitaries U and V.

title: Polar decomposition
establishes: Every operator T equals U|T| with |T| = sqrt(T^dagger T) and U unitary, |T| is unique and U is unique on the image of |T|, and a map V -> W has the same form with U a partial isometry, where a partial isometry is a map that is isometric on (ker U)^perp and zero on ker U.

title: Maps with the same Gram operator differ by an isometry
establishes: For maps A: K -> V and B: K' -> V, A A^dagger = B B^dagger iff A = B W for a partial isometry W: K -> K' with final space (ker B)^perp; W can then be taken with initial space (ker A)^perp; and when dim K = dim K', in particular for K = C^m and K' = C^m' after appending zero columns so that m = m', A A^dagger = B B^dagger iff A = B U for a unitary U.

title: Positive and negative parts of a self-adjoint operator
establishes: Every self-adjoint A is A_+ - A_- with positive parts supported on orthogonal subspaces, and the maximum of tr(EA) over effects 0 <= E <= I is tr A_+, attained at the projector onto the positive eigenspace.

title: The trace norm
establishes: ||A||_1 = tr|A| equals the sum of the singular values of A, is zero only at A = 0, satisfies ||cA||_1 = |c| ||A||_1, and is unchanged by A -> UAV for unitaries U and V.

title: Trace norm and operator norm in duality
establishes: |tr(XA)| <= ||X|| ||A||_1, so ||A||_1 = max over unitaries U of |tr(UA)|, hence ||A + B||_1 <= ||A||_1 + ||B||_1, so ||.||_1 is a norm, and for self-adjoint A, ||A||_1 = tr A_+ + tr A_- = max over -I <= X <= I of tr(XA).

title: The Powers-Stormer inequality
establishes: For positive A and B, ||sqrt A - sqrt B||_2^2 <= ||A - B||_1, proved by evaluating tr((A - B) S), with S the sign of sqrt A - sqrt B, in the eigenbasis of sqrt A - sqrt B.

title: Problems for Part X
establishes: Integrated problems on square roots, polar decompositions, singular values and trace norms of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Compactness and convexity in finite dimensions
goal: Build continuity and compactness in R^n, convex sets, Caratheodory, separation, extreme points, polytopes (with the bounded solution sets of linear inequalities) and Jensen's inequality, which mixed states, Bell polytopes and entropy use.

title: Bounded sequences in R^n have convergent subsequences
establishes: Every bounded sequence in R^n, and hence in C^n or in a space of matrices, has a convergent subsequence.

title: Continuity in R^n via sequences
establishes: f: D -> R^m on D inside R^n is continuous at x in D iff f(x_n) -> f(x) for every sequence x_n in D with x_n -> x; sums, products and compositions of continuous functions are continuous; norms, inner products, matrix entries and x -> <x,Ax> are continuous; and coordinates in an orthonormal basis identify every n-dimensional real inner-product space, in particular the self-adjoint operators with tr(AB), with R^n preserving norms, so every result of this Part holds there.

title: Closed bounded sets and the extreme value theorem
establishes: A continuous real function on a closed bounded subset of R^n attains its maximum and minimum, and continuous images of closed bounded sets are closed and bounded.

title: Convex sets, convex combinations and convex hulls
establishes: A set is convex iff it contains all finite convex combinations of its points, the convex hull of S is the set of all convex combinations of points of S, and a point is extreme iff it is not the midpoint of two distinct points of the set.

title: Caratheodory's theorem
establishes: Every point in the convex hull of S in R^n is a convex combination of at most n+1 points of S, so the convex hull of a closed bounded set is closed and bounded.

title: Closest points and the separating hyperplane theorem
establishes: A closed convex set C in R^n has a unique point closest to any x, and if x is not in C there are a linear functional f and a number c with f(x) > c >= f(y) for all y in C.

title: Interior and boundary points of convex sets
establishes: A point of S in R^n is interior if some ball about it lies in S, and is a boundary point otherwise; a convex set either lies in an affine hyperplane, which is isometric to R^(n-1), or has an interior point; and a line through an interior point of a closed bounded convex set meets the set in a segment whose endpoints are boundary points.
note: Interior point: if S is not in a hyperplane it contains n+1 affinely independent points, and the open simplex they span contains a ball. Segment: the intersection with the line is closed, bounded and convex, hence an interval; points beyond its ends lie outside S.

title: Supporting hyperplanes
establishes: Every boundary point of a closed convex set in R^n lies on a supporting hyperplane, one with the whole set on one side, obtained as a limit of separating hyperplanes for points outside the set.

title: Extreme points and Minkowski's theorem
establishes: A closed bounded convex set in R^n is the convex hull of its extreme points, proved by induction on dimension using supporting hyperplanes.

title: Polytopes, vertices and facet inequalities
establishes: The convex hull of finitely many points is a polytope whose extreme points are among those points, and a linear inequality holds on a polytope iff it holds at every vertex.
gap: Omitted: the direction polytope => finite intersection of half-spaces of the Minkowski-Weyl theorem. Why: the converse direction for bounded sets, which is the one used, is proved in bounded-constraint-polytopes and applied in no-signalling-polytope and pr-box; the omitted direction is a long Fourier-Motzkin argument and nothing uses it. Where: G. M. Ziegler, Lectures on Polytopes, Thm 1.1.

title: Bounded solution sets of linear inequalities are polytopes
establishes: A bounded set in R^n defined by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities has finitely many extreme points, since x is extreme iff no nonzero direction d keeps every constraint tight at x tight along x +- d, so each extreme point is the unique solution of some subset of constraints made equalities; by Minkowski's theorem the set is the convex hull of these points, a polytope.
note: If the tight constraints at x leave a nonzero direction d, x +- eps d stays feasible for small eps because the slack constraints are strict, so x is not extreme.

title: Convex functions and Jensen's inequality
establishes: A twice-differentiable function with nonnegative second derivative is convex, by the mean value theorem, and a convex f satisfies f(sum p_i x_i) <= sum p_i f(x_i), strictly when f'' > 0 and the x_i with p_i > 0 are not all equal.

title: Problems for Part XI
establishes: Integrated problems on hulls, extreme points and separation in the plane, in R^3 and in the space of 2x2 self-adjoint matrices, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Direct sums and tensor products
goal: Construct direct sums and tensor products, operators on them, the partial trace with its uniqueness property, the partial transpose, the Schmidt decomposition and purification, all as mathematics.

title: External direct sums of inner-product spaces and block operators
establishes: V (+) W with <(v,w),(v',w')> = <v,v'> + <w,w'> is an inner-product space of dimension dim V + dim W containing V and W as orthogonal complements, and operators on it are 2x2 block matrices of maps.

title: Bilinear maps
establishes: A bilinear map on V x W is fixed by its values on pairs of basis vectors, and the bilinear maps V x W -> U form a space of dimension (dim V)(dim W)(dim U).

title: The tensor product of two vector spaces: construction
establishes: Given bases (e_i) of V and (f_j) of W, the space with basis symbols e_i (x) f_j and the bilinear map (v,w) -> v (x) w defined by expansion has dimension (dim V)(dim W), and every element is a sum of products v (x) w.

title: The universal property of the tensor product
establishes: Every bilinear map out of V x W factors uniquely through a linear map on V (x) W, so the tensor product built from one pair of bases is canonically isomorphic to the one built from any other.

title: The tensor product of inner-product spaces
establishes: <v (x) w, v' (x) w'> = <v,v'><w,w'> extends to a unique inner product on V (x) W for which products of orthonormal bases are orthonormal bases, and C^2 (x) C^2 is identified with C^4.

title: Tensor products of operators and the Kronecker product
establishes: (A (x) B)(v (x) w) = Av (x) Bw defines an operator with (A (x) B)(C (x) D) = AC (x) BD, (A (x) B)^dagger = A^dagger (x) B^dagger and tr(A (x) B) = tr A tr B, whose matrix is the Kronecker product and whose eigenvalues are products of eigenvalues, so tensor products preserve self-adjointness, unitarity, positivity and projectors.
note: Eigenvalues: if A and B are upper triangular in bases (e_i) and (f_j), A (x) B is upper triangular in the lexicographically ordered basis e_i (x) f_j with diagonal a_ii b_jj.

title: Every operator on a tensor product is a sum of products
establishes: L(V (x) W) = L(V) (x) L(W): every operator on V (x) W is a sum of products A_k (x) B_k, and the Pauli products sigma_j (x) sigma_k divided by 2 form a Hilbert-Schmidt orthonormal basis for two qubits.

title: Vectors in V (x) W as matrices
establishes: psi = sum psi_ij e_i (x) f_j corresponds to its coefficient matrix [psi_ij], and psi is a product vector iff this matrix has rank 1; with the unnormalised Omega_V = sum_i e_i (x) e_i in V (x) V, (A (x) I) Omega_V = (I (x) A^T) Omega_V for A on V, <(A (x) I) Omega_V, (B (x) I) Omega_V> = tr(A^dagger B), and every vector of V (x) W is (I (x) M) Omega_V for a unique linear M: V -> W.

title: Tensor products of several spaces and permutation operators
establishes: Tensor products are associative up to canonical isomorphism, so n qubits live in C^(2^n) with the binary-string basis, permuting factors defines unitary operators, and the swap on V (x) V has eigenvalues +1 and -1 on the symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces.

title: The partial trace
establishes: tr_B(A (x) B) = (tr B) A extends linearly to a well-defined map L(V (x) W) -> L(V), equal to sum_j (I (x) <f_j|) M (I (x) |f_j>) for any orthonormal basis (f_j) of W.

title: The partial trace is the unique map compatible with local operators
establishes: tr_B is the only linear map L: L(V (x) W) -> L(V) with tr(L(M) X) = tr(M (X (x) I)) for all X in L(V) and all M, by Riesz in the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product.

title: Properties of the partial trace
establishes: tr_B is positive and trace preserving, tr_B((X (x) I) M (Y (x) I)) = X tr_B(M) Y, tr_B((I (x) Y) M) = tr_B(M (I (x) Y)) for every Y on W (so tr_B((I (x) U) M (I (x) U^dagger)) = tr_B(M) for unitary U), partial traces over different factors of a threefold product commute, and for positive M, (P (x) I) M (P (x) I) = M, where P is the orthogonal projector onto the image of tr_B M (its support).
note: Support lemma: tr(((I-P) (x) I) M) = tr((I-P) tr_B M) = 0 with M >= 0 forces M((I-P) (x) I) = 0.

title: The transpose and the partial transpose
establishes: The transpose in a fixed basis preserves trace and spectrum, but the partial transpose of |Omega><Omega| on C^2 (x) C^2 is the swap, which has eigenvalue -1, so for |Phi+> = Omega/sqrt2 it has eigenvalue -1/2 and partial transposition does not preserve positivity.

title: The Schmidt decomposition
establishes: Every unit vector in V (x) W is sum_k s_k e_k (x) f_k with s_k > 0, sum s_k^2 = 1 and orthonormal (e_k), (f_k), obtained from the SVD of its coefficient matrix, and the s_k^2 are the nonzero eigenvalues of both partial traces of its projector.

title: Every positive unit-trace operator is a partial trace of a rank-one projector
establishes: For every positive rho on V with tr rho = 1 and every W with dim W >= rank rho there is a unit vector psi in V (x) W with tr_W |psi><psi| = rho, and any two such vectors in the same V (x) W differ by a unitary on W.

title: Problems for Part XII
establishes: Integrated problems on two- and three-qubit tensor products, partial traces and Schmidt decompositions, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Composite systems and density operators
goal: State the composite-system postulate, meet product and entangled states, and derive density operators from ensembles, with their convex geometry and the unitary freedom of ensembles.

title: The composite-system postulate
establishes: Postulate: the Hilbert space of a pair of systems is H_A (x) H_B, a local observable A is represented by A (x) I, and on product states the outcomes of local measurements are independent with the single-system distributions.

title: Product and entangled pure states
establishes: A pure state of AB is a product iff its coefficient matrix has rank 1, every pair of local observables is uncorrelated in a product state, and (|00> + |11>)/sqrt2 has perfectly correlated sigma_z outcomes.

title: Two-qubit gates
establishes: CNOT and CZ are unitary and are not products of one-qubit unitaries, and CNOT maps the product state |+>|0> to an entangled state.

title: The Bell basis and the Bell measurement
establishes: The four Bell states form an orthonormal basis of C^2 (x) C^2, each is (sigma_k (x) I)|Phi+> up to a global phase, (U (x) I)|Phi+> = (I (x) U^T)|Phi+>, and CNOT followed by a Hadamard on the control qubit maps the Bell basis to the computational basis, which realises a Bell measurement.

title: Spin correlations in the singlet state
establishes: In the singlet the outcomes of sigma.a on A and sigma.b on B have correlation E(a,b) = -a.b, each local outcome is uniformly random, and (U (x) U)|Psi-> = det(U)|Psi-> for every unitary U on C^2.

title: Ensembles and the density operator
establishes: For an ensemble {p_i, psi_i}, every measurement's outcome probabilities are tr(rho P_k) with rho = sum p_i |psi_i><psi_i|, so two ensembles with the same rho cannot be told apart by any measurement.

title: Density operators are the positive operators of unit trace
establishes: An operator arises from some ensemble iff it is positive with trace 1, and its spectral decomposition gives one such ensemble of orthogonal states.

title: Pure and mixed states as extreme and non-extreme points
establishes: The density operators form a closed bounded convex set whose extreme points are exactly the rank-one projectors, and rho is pure iff tr(rho^2) = 1.

title: The Bloch ball
establishes: Qubit density operators are exactly (I + r.sigma)/2 with |r| <= 1, with eigenvalues (1 +- |r|)/2 and purity (1 + |r|^2)/2, and unitary evolution acts on r by the rotations of SO(3).

title: One density operator, many ensembles: the qubit case
establishes: A qubit state with Bloch vector r inside the ball is a mixture of the two pure states at the ends of every chord of the sphere through r, with weights fixed by where r divides the chord, so one density operator has infinitely many ensembles.

title: Evolution and measurement of density operators
establishes: Unitary evolution acts as rho -> U rho U^dagger, a projective measurement gives outcome k with probability tr(P_k rho) and state P_k rho P_k/tr(P_k rho), and forgetting the outcome gives sum_k P_k rho P_k.

title: The unitary freedom in ensemble decompositions
establishes: Two lists of unnormalised vectors {psi_i} and {phi_j} give the same density operator iff psi_i = sum_j u_ij phi_j for a unitary matrix u, after padding the shorter list with zero vectors.

title: Problems for Part XIII
establishes: Integrated problems on product and entangled states, Bell measurements and ensembles of qubit density operators, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Reduced states, purification and entanglement
goal: Derive reduced states from the uniqueness of the partial trace, then the Schmidt form, purification, steering, separability, the partial-transpose test, Werner states and witnesses.

title: Reduced states
establishes: The statistics of all local measurements on A of a state rho_AB are those of tr_B(rho_AB), by the uniqueness of the partial trace this is the only density operator on A with that property, and it transforms as U rho_A U^dagger under local unitaries U (x) V.

title: Reduced states of Bell states and product states
establishes: Each half of a Bell state is the maximally mixed state I/2, so no measurement on one half alone distinguishes the four Bell states, and a pure state of AB is a product iff its reduced states are pure.

title: The Schmidt form and purification of bipartite states
establishes: Every pure state of AB has a Schmidt form sum_k sqrt(lambda_k) |a_k>|b_k>, so its two reduced states have the same nonzero spectrum and the Schmidt rank, unchanged by local unitaries, is 1 exactly for product states; and, by purification-math, every density operator on A is the reduced state of a pure state on A (x) R whenever dim R >= rank rho, any two purifications into the same R differing by a unitary on R alone.

title: Every ensemble is prepared by a measurement on a purification
establishes: For a purification of rho_A on A (x) R, each ensemble decomposition of rho_A with m members is obtained, with its probabilities, by a projective measurement on R followed by conditioning on its outcome, provided dim R >= m (the Schrodinger-HJW theorem).

title: Separable mixed states
establishes: A density operator on AB is separable if it is a convex combination of product states, the separable states form a closed bounded convex set by Caratheodory's theorem, and every separable state can be prepared by local operations coordinated by shared random numbers.

title: The partial-transpose criterion
establishes: If rho_AB is separable then its partial transpose is positive, so a negative eigenvalue of the partial transpose certifies entanglement.
gap: Omitted: the converse in dimensions 2x2 and 2x3 (a PPT state there is separable) and its failure in larger dimensions. Why: it relies on the Stormer-Woronowicz classification of positive maps on low-dimensional matrix algebras, a long separate theory; the book uses the converse nowhere, and the Werner threshold is proved directly. Where: M., P. and R. Horodecki, Phys. Lett. A 223, 1 (1996), with E. Stormer, Acta Math. 110, 233 (1963) for 2x2 and S. L. Woronowicz, Rep. Math. Phys. 10, 165 (1976) for 2x3.
note: Credit the criterion to A. Peres, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 1413 (1996).

title: Two-qubit Werner states
establishes: The state p|Psi-><Psi-| + (1-p) I/4 is entangled exactly when p > 1/3: entangled above 1/3 by the partial transpose, and separable at and below 1/3 because at p = 1/3 it equals the average of |n><n| (x) |-n><-n| over the six directions +-x, +-y, +-z.

title: Entanglement witnesses
establishes: For every entangled rho there is a self-adjoint W with tr(W sigma) >= 0 for all separable sigma and tr(W rho) < 0, by the separating hyperplane theorem in the real inner-product space of self-adjoint operators.

title: Problems for Part XIV
establishes: Integrated problems on reduced states, Schmidt forms, steering and separability of two-qubit states, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Entropy
goal: Build Shannon entropy, relative entropy and mutual information, then von Neumann entropy, Klein's inequality, subadditivity and the entanglement entropy of pure states.

title: Shannon entropy
establishes: H(p) = -sum p_i log p_i, with log natural (entropies in nats), satisfies 0 <= H(p) <= log n, with H = 0 exactly for deterministic p and H = log n exactly for the uniform distribution; log_2 gives bits, and h(q) = -q log_2 q - (1-q) log_2(1-q) is the binary entropy.

title: Relative entropy and Gibbs' inequality
establishes: D(p||q) = sum p_i log(p_i/q_i) is nonnegative and zero only when p = q, by log x <= x - 1 with equality only at x = 1.

title: Joint and conditional entropy, mutual information and subadditivity
establishes: H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X), H(Y|X) >= 0, and I(X:Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) = D(p_XY || p_X p_Y) >= 0 with equality iff X and Y are independent.

title: The von Neumann entropy
establishes: S(rho) = -tr(rho log rho) equals the Shannon entropy of the eigenvalues of rho, is unitarily invariant, lies between 0 and log d with S = 0 iff rho is pure and S = log d iff rho = I/d, and is additive on tensor products.

title: Klein's inequality
establishes: For density operators rho and sigma, S(rho||sigma) = tr(rho log rho) - tr(rho log sigma) >= 0 when supp rho is inside supp sigma, with log taken on the support (and S = +infinity otherwise), with equality iff rho = sigma, proved by expanding in both eigenbases, using the doubly stochastic matrix |<e_i|f_j>|^2, Jensen's inequality for the concave log, and Gibbs' inequality.

title: Subadditivity and the Araki-Lieb inequality
establishes: For a density operator rho_AB, |S(rho_A) - S(rho_B)| <= S(rho_AB) <= S(rho_A) + S(rho_B), the upper bound from Klein's inequality with sigma = rho_A (x) rho_B, whose support contains that of rho_AB by the support lemma for the partial trace, and log(rho_A (x) rho_B) = log rho_A (x) I + I (x) log rho_B on that support, and the lower bound from a purification, and I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(AB) equals 2 S(A) for pure states.

title: Concavity of the von Neumann entropy
establishes: S(sum_i p_i rho_i) >= sum_i p_i S(rho_i), from subadditivity applied to the block-diagonal operator sum_i p_i rho_i (x) |i><i|.

title: The entanglement entropy of a bipartite pure state
establishes: E(psi) = S(rho_A) = S(rho_B) is the Shannon entropy of the Schmidt coefficients, is invariant under local unitaries, vanishes exactly for product states, and equals log d exactly when the reduced state is I/d.
gap: Omitted: the operational characterisation of E as the asymptotic rate of conversion to and from Bell pairs by local operations and classical communication. Why: it needs asymptotic typicality arguments not developed here. Where: C. H. Bennett, H. J. Bernstein, S. Popescu, B. Schumacher, Phys. Rev. A 53, 2046 (1996); M. Wilde, Quantum Information Theory, 2nd ed., Ch. 19.

title: Problems for Part XV
establishes: Integrated problems computing entropies, mutual informations and entanglement entropies of two- and three-qubit states, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Probability II: concentration, Markov processes and densities
goal: Prove Hoeffding's and Azuma's inequalities for hypothesis tests, build Markov chains, the Bayes filter and master equations, and add densities on an interval, the uniform distribution on the sphere and the Poisson limit.

title: Hoeffding's lemma
establishes: If X takes values in [a,b] and E[X] = 0 then E[exp(sX)] <= exp(s^2 (b-a)^2/8) for every real s, by bounding exp on [a,b] by its chord and applying Taylor's theorem to the logarithm of the resulting bound.

title: Hoeffding's inequality
establishes: For n independent variables with values in [a,b], the mean exceeds its expectation by t with probability at most exp(-2 n t^2/(b-a)^2), by Markov's inequality applied to exp(s times the sum) and optimising s.

title: Hypothesis tests and p-values
establishes: A test rejects a null hypothesis when a statistic is extreme, its p-value bounds the probability under every model of the null of a result at least as extreme, and Hoeffding's inequality gives such bounds assuming nothing beyond independence and boundedness.

title: Martingale differences and the Azuma-Hoeffding inequality
establishes: If the conditional expectation of each increment given the past is at most zero and each increment lies in an interval of length c, the sum after n steps exceeds t with probability at most exp(-2 t^2/(n c^2)), with no independence assumed.

title: Stochastic matrices and discrete-time Markov chains
establishes: A Markov chain on a finite set is given by a column-stochastic matrix, distributions evolve by p_{n+1} = T p_n, and stochastic matrices are exactly the linear maps that send probability vectors to probability vectors.

title: Hidden Markov models and the Bayes filter
establishes: For a hidden Markov chain observed through noisy outputs, the posterior over the hidden state after each observation is obtained recursively by a prediction step with T and a Bayes update with the likelihood of the observation.

title: Rate matrices and the master equation
establishes: A matrix Q with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero column sums generates stochastic matrices exp(tQ) for t >= 0, and p(t) = exp(tQ)p(0) is the unique solution of the master equation dp/dt = Qp.
gap: Omitted: the construction of the jump process itself (random paths with exponentially distributed waiting times between jumps) from the rates. Why: it needs probability on infinite path spaces, and the book uses only the master equation that the distribution obeys. Where: J. R. Norris, Markov Chains (1997), Secs 2.6-2.8.

title: Master equations with time-dependent rates
establishes: For continuous rates Q(t), any solution of dp/dt = Q(t)p starting from a probability vector remains a probability vector (column sums by 1^T Q = 0, nonnegativity by Gronwall applied to sum_i (min(p_i,0))^2), and there is at most one solution with a given initial distribution.

title: Probability densities on an interval
establishes: A nonnegative continuous (or piecewise-continuous) density with integral one assigns probabilities to subintervals and expectations to piecewise-continuous functions, and the rules of finite probability hold for finite unions of intervals.
gap: Omitted: probability measures on general (Borel) events. Why: measure theory is beyond the book, and only interval events are used. Where: P. Billingsley, Probability and Measure, 3rd ed., Chs 1-2.

title: The uniform distribution on the unit sphere
establishes: Taking z uniform on [-1,1] and phi uniform on [0, 2 pi), independently, defines a random unit vector lambda = (sqrt(1-z^2) cos phi, sqrt(1-z^2) sin phi, z) whose law is unchanged by every rotation, so a.lambda is uniform on [-1,1] for every unit vector a and E[f(a.lambda, b.lambda)] depends on a and b only through a.b (Archimedes' hat-box theorem).
gap: Omitted: the proof that this law is rotation invariant, that is, that it is normalised surface area on S^2, and the double integrals over (z, phi) that define its expectations. Why: both need surface area and the change-of-variables formula in two dimensions, which the book does not build; only the stated invariance is used, by werner-local-model and ks-qubit-model. Where: M. Spivak, Calculus on Manifolds, Chs 3 and 5; for the hat-box theorem, Archimedes, On the Sphere and Cylinder I.

title: The Poisson process as a limit of Bernoulli trials
establishes: If an event occurs with probability lambda dt in each of t/dt independent steps, then as dt -> 0, P(k events) -> exp(-lambda t)(lambda t)^k/k! for each k, using |log(1+x) - x| <= x^2/(2(1-|x|)^2) from Taylor's theorem, and these limits sum to 1 by the exponential series; and the waiting time T to the first event satisfies P(T > s) = (1 - lambda dt)^(s/dt) -> exp(-lambda s) for every s >= 0, so P(a < T <= b) -> integral_a^b lambda exp(-lambda u) du for all 0 <= a < b.

title: Problems for Part XVI
establishes: Integrated problems on concentration bounds, p-values, Bayes filters and master equations, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: General measurements and channels
goal: Derive POVMs twice, from an ancilla and from affine statistics, then dilate them; build complete positivity, the Choi-Kraus cycle, Stinespring, instruments and their probe realisation.

title: Measuring a system through an ancilla
establishes: Coupling a system to an ancilla in a fixed state by a unitary and measuring the ancilla projectively gives outcome k with probability tr(E_k rho) for positive operators E_k on the system with sum_k E_k = I.

title: Positive operator-valued measures
establishes: A POVM is a list of effects summing to I; the unsharp spin observable (I +- s m.sigma)/2, the qubit trine and the tetrahedral (SIC) POVM are examples that are not projective, and the SIC is informationally complete, rho = sum_k (3 p_k - 1/2) Pi_k with Pi_k its rank-one projectors.

title: Affine maps on states extend to linear functionals
establishes: A map from density operators to real numbers that preserves convex mixtures extends uniquely to a real-linear functional on the self-adjoint operators.

title: POVMs are the general form of measurement statistics
establishes: Every map from density operators to probability distributions on a finite outcome set that preserves convex mixtures has the form rho -> tr(rho E_k) for unique effects E_k summing to I.

title: Naimark's dilation theorem
establishes: For every POVM {E_k} on H the map V psi = sum_k sqrt(E_k) psi (x) |k> is an isometry with E_k = V^dagger (I (x) |k><k|) V, so every POVM is a projective measurement on a larger system after an isometric, hence unitary, coupling.

title: Naimark dilation by direct sum
establishes: Equivalently, every POVM is E_k = P_H Q_k P_H for orthogonal projectors Q_k summing to I on a direct sum H (+) K, with P_H the projector onto H.

title: Linear maps on operators: positivity, trace preservation and the adjoint
establishes: A linear map Phi: L(H_A) -> L(H_B) sends density operators to density operators iff it is positive and trace preserving, it has a unique Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint, trace preserving iff the adjoint is unital, and the transpose is such a map.

title: Complete positivity
establishes: Because an operation on A must still give states when A is part of AR, physical maps must be completely positive (id_R (x) Phi positive for every R), and the transpose is positive but not completely positive.

title: The Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism
establishes: Phi -> J(Phi) = sum_ij |i><j| (x) Phi(|i><j|) is a linear bijection from maps L(H_A) -> L(H_B) to operators on H_A (x) H_B, with Phi(X) recovered from J by a partial trace, and Phi is trace preserving iff tr_B J(Phi) = I.

title: Choi's theorem I: a completely positive map has a positive Choi operator
establishes: If Phi is completely positive then J(Phi) >= 0, and every map of the form X -> sum_k K_k X K_k^dagger is completely positive.

title: Choi's theorem II: the Kraus representation
establishes: If J(Phi) >= 0, a spectral decomposition of J(Phi) gives Phi(X) = sum_k K_k X K_k^dagger with at most d_A d_B operators, which closes the cycle (completely positive iff J(Phi) >= 0 iff Kraus form), and Phi is trace preserving iff sum_k K_k^dagger K_k = I.

title: Freedom in the Kraus representation
establishes: Two Kraus lists {K_k} and {L_j} give the same map iff L_j = sum_k u_jk K_k for a unitary u, after padding the shorter list with zeros.

title: The Stinespring dilation
establishes: Every channel is Phi(rho) = tr_E(V rho V^dagger) for an isometry V: H_A -> H_B (x) H_E with dim H_E <= d_A d_B, equivalently a unitary interaction with an environment in a fixed pure state followed by discarding, unique up to an isometry on E.

title: Composing, tensoring and discarding channels
establishes: Compositions, tensor products and convex combinations of channels are channels, and appending a fixed state and taking a partial trace are channels.

title: The complementary channel
establishes: Tracing out the output instead of the environment in a Stinespring dilation gives the complementary channel, determined by Phi up to an isometry on E.

title: Channels in the Heisenberg picture
establishes: The dual map Phi^dagger, defined by tr(Phi(rho) X) = tr(rho Phi^dagger(X)), has Kraus operators K_k^dagger, is completely positive and unital, and sends POVMs to POVMs.

title: Qubit channels I: unitary, dephasing and depolarising
establishes: These channels have explicit Kraus lists and act on the Bloch vector as a rotation, a contraction of the x and y components, and a uniform contraction.

title: Qubit channels II: amplitude damping, erasure and measure-and-prepare
establishes: Amplitude damping has Kraus operators [[1,0],[0,sqrt(1-g)]] and [[0,sqrt g],[0,0]] and moves every Bloch vector toward |0> by the affine map r -> M r + c, erasure maps into a larger space, and measure-and-prepare channels rho -> sum_k tr(E_k rho) sigma_k have Choi operator sum_k E_k^T (x) sigma_k, which is separable, and for a basis measurement {|e_k>} with pure preparations phi_k their Kraus operators are |phi_k><e_k|.

title: Instruments
establishes: An instrument is a list of completely positive maps Phi_k whose sum is trace preserving; outcome k occurs with probability tr Phi_k(rho), the state becomes Phi_k(rho)/tr Phi_k(rho), its POVM is E_k = Phi_k^dagger(I), and the Luders instrument is one of many with a given POVM.

title: Every instrument is a Luders measurement followed by outcome-dependent channels
establishes: Every instrument with POVM {E_k} is Phi_k = C_k o L_k, where L_k(rho) = sqrt(E_k) rho sqrt(E_k) and each C_k is a channel. Proof: stack the Kraus operators of Phi_k into one map K_k = sum_j K_kj (x) |j>: H -> H (x) C^m, so K_k^dagger K_k = E_k; polar-decompose it as K_k = W_k sqrt(E_k) with W_k a partial isometry; then set C_k(s) = tr_{C^m}(W_k s W_k^dagger) + tr((I - W_k^dagger W_k) s) tau for a fixed state tau.

title: Every instrument is realised by a probe
establishes: Every instrument arises from preparing a probe in a fixed pure state, applying a unitary to system and probe, and measuring a projective pointer observable on the probe, which generalises Naimark's theorem from POVMs to instruments (Ozawa 1984).

title: Channels generated by random jumps: master equations of Lindblad type
establishes: If in each time dt a channel Phi is applied with probability lambda dt and otherwise exp(-iH dt/hbar) acts, the averaged state obeys d rho/dt = -(i/hbar)[H,rho] + lambda(Phi(rho) - rho), whose solution maps are channels for all t >= 0, as limits of compositions of channels, because complete positivity and trace preservation are closed conditions.

title: Problems for Part XVII
establishes: Integrated problems on Naimark dilations, Choi operators, Kraus lists and instruments for qubits and qutrits, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Entanglement and information
goal: Prove no-signalling and no-cloning, run teleportation, build the trace distance, Helstrom bound and fidelity, and derive information-disturbance from them, then treat BB84 and monogamy, with BB84 security and the Coffman-Kundu-Wootters inequality as labelled gaps.

title: The no-signalling theorem
establishes: Whatever instrument is applied on B, the reduced state of A averaged over B's outcomes is unchanged, so no choice made at B alters any statistics at A.

title: The no-cloning theorem
establishes: No channel maps psi to psi (x) psi for two distinct non-orthogonal pure states, because in a Stinespring dilation <psi|phi> = <psi|phi>^2 <e_psi|e_phi> forces the overlap to be 0 or of modulus 1, while orthogonal states can be copied.

title: Quantum teleportation
establishes: With a shared |Phi+>, a Bell measurement by A and two classical bits allow B to recover an unknown qubit state exactly by a Pauli correction, and before the bits arrive B's state is I/2, as no-signalling requires.

title: Entanglement swapping
establishes: A Bell measurement on one half of each of two Bell pairs leaves the two other halves, which never interacted, in a Bell state labelled by the outcome.

title: The trace distance between states
establishes: T(rho,sigma) = (1/2)||rho - sigma||_1 is a metric on density operators equal to the maximum over effects of tr(E(rho - sigma)), it is half the Euclidean distance of the Bloch vectors for qubits, and sqrt(1 - |<psi|phi>|^2) for pure states.

title: The Helstrom bound
establishes: The highest probability of correctly identifying which of rho_0, rho_1 (prior probabilities p_0, p_1) was prepared is (1 + ||p_0 rho_0 - p_1 rho_1||_1)/2, attained by projecting onto the positive part, so non-orthogonal pure states can never be identified with certainty.

title: Channels do not increase trace distance
establishes: For every channel Phi, T(Phi(rho), Phi(sigma)) <= T(rho, sigma), in particular for the partial trace, because the dual of a channel maps effects to effects.

title: Fidelity and Uhlmann's theorem
establishes: F(rho,sigma) = ||sqrt(rho) sqrt(sigma)||_1 equals the maximum of |<psi|phi>| over purifications psi of rho and phi of sigma on a common space, so 0 <= F <= 1, F = 1 iff rho = sigma, and F = |<psi|phi>| for pure states.

title: Channels do not decrease fidelity
establishes: F(Phi(rho), Phi(sigma)) >= F(rho, sigma) for every channel, because a Stinespring isometry maps purifications of rho and sigma to purifications of their images with the same overlap.

title: The Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities I: the upper bound
establishes: T(rho,sigma) <= sqrt(1 - F(rho,sigma)^2), with equality for pure states, from the pure-state formula for purifications attaining F and contractivity of T under the partial trace.

title: The Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities II: the lower bound
