establishes: 1 - F(rho,sigma) <= T(rho,sigma), because F >= tr(sqrt(rho) sqrt(sigma)) = 1 - (1/2)||sqrt(rho) - sqrt(sigma)||_2^2 and the Powers-Stormer inequality bounds the last norm by ||rho - sigma||_1.

title: No information gain without disturbance
establishes: If an interaction with an environment leaves each of two non-orthogonal pure states of the system unchanged, the environment ends in the same state for both inputs, so no measurement on the environment learns which state was sent.

title: A computed information-disturbance trade-off for two qubit states
establishes: For two equiprobable qubit states with Bloch vectors (sin a, 0, +-cos a) and the instrument with Kraus operators sqrt((I +- s Z)/2), the probability of guessing which state was sent rises with s while the fidelity of the post-measurement state with the input falls, along a curve computed in closed form.
gap: Omitted: the proof that this family is optimal among all instruments for the trade-off. Why: the optimisation over all instruments is long and is not used later. Where: F. Buscemi and M. F. Sacchi, Phys. Rev. A 74, 052320 (2006), derive the optimal trade-off between average success probability and fidelity-based disturbance for two equiprobable pure states; C. A. Fuchs and A. Peres, Phys. Rev. A 53, 2038 (1996), treat the mutual-information version, partly numerically.

title: The BB84 protocol and the intercept-resend attack
establishes: In BB84 an eavesdropper who measures each qubit in a random one of the two bases and resends her result causes an error rate of 1/4 on the sifted key, which the legitimate parties detect, with a stated confidence, by comparing a random sample.

title: Why disturbance limits the eavesdropper in BB84
establishes: By the information-disturbance trade-off, every attack that gives the eavesdropper information about the key bits produces errors, and for observed error rates below about 11% error correction and privacy amplification yield a secret key at rate 1 - 2h(Q).
gap: Omitted: the proof of security against general (coherent) attacks and the key rate 1 - 2h(Q), which need entropic uncertainty relations or de Finetti theorems and privacy amplification. Why: each is a separate theory. Where: P. W. Shor, J. Preskill, Phys. Rev. Lett. 85, 441 (2000); R. Renner, PhD thesis, ETH Zurich (2005), arXiv:quant-ph/0512258.

title: Monogamy of entanglement for pure states
establishes: If rho_AB is pure then every state of ABC with that marginal equals rho_AB (x) rho_C, so a system maximally entangled with one partner is uncorrelated with every other system.

title: The Coffman-Kundu-Wootters inequality
establishes: With C(psi) = 2|ad - bc| for a pure two-qubit state a|00> + b|01> + c|10> + d|11> and C(rho) the infimum over ensembles of rho of the average of C(psi_i), the pure-state tangle is tau_A(BC) = 4 det rho_A; three qubits satisfy C_AB^2 + C_AC^2 <= tau_A(BC) (stated); for GHZ tau_A(BC) = 1 while both marginals are separable, so C_AB = C_AC = 0; for W every ensemble of rho_AB has average concurrence 2/3, so C_AB = C_AC = 2/3 and equality holds at 8/9.
gap: Omitted: Wootters' closed formula for the concurrence of mixed two-qubit states, and the proof of C_AB^2 + C_AC^2 <= tau_A(BC), which rests on it. Why: the formula's proof is a long optimisation over ensembles. Where: W. K. Wootters, Phys. Rev. Lett. 80, 2245 (1998); V. Coffman, J. Kundu, W. K. Wootters, Phys. Rev. A 61, 052306 (2000).
note: W: rho_AB = (1/3)|00><00| + (2/3)|Psi+><Psi+|; ensemble vectors lie in its range, a|00> + b|Psi+> has 2|det| = |b|^2, and C is homogeneous of degree 2, so every ensemble averages <Psi+|rho_AB|Psi+> = 2/3.

title: Problems for Part XVIII
establishes: Integrated problems on teleportation variants, state discrimination, fidelity bounds and eavesdropping on BB84, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Measurement, disturbance and feedback (Q1)
goal: Model measurement as interaction with a probe and derive what one interaction can learn and what it must change: strength, duality, Zeno, QND, the Wigner-Araki-Yanase limit, weak values, joint measurability, error-disturbance relations, filtering, feedback and Leggett-Garg.

title: Von Neumann's pre-measurement model
establishes: A unitary coupling with U(psi (x) m_0) = sum_k P_k psi (x) m_k and orthonormal pointer states, followed by reading the pointer, reproduces the Born probabilities and the Luders state update for the observable sum_k a_k P_k, and erases the system's coherences between different P_k.

title: Measurement strength: pointer states that overlap
establishes: With qubit pointer states of overlap <m_0|m_1> = c, the induced instrument interpolates between no measurement (c = 1) and a projective one (c = 0): the pointer's Helstrom bias is sqrt(1 - |c|^2) and the system's coherence |rho_01| is multiplied by |c|.

title: Fringe visibility with a which-path detector
establishes: In a balanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer whose path j applies a unitary U_j to a detector initially in rho_D, the fringe visibility is V = |tr(U_2 rho_D U_1^dagger)|, which equals |<d_1|d_2>| for pure rho_D = |d><d|, with d_j = U_j d.

title: Englert's duality relation
establishes: Path distinguishability D (the trace distance of the detector states) and fringe visibility V satisfy D^2 + V^2 <= 1, with equality for pure detector states, proved by purifying the detector, using D^2 + V^2 = 1 for the pure case, and contractivity of the trace distance under the partial trace.

title: Experiment: the which-way atom interferometer
establishes: Durr, Nonn and Rempe (Nature 395, 33, 1998; PRL 81, 5705, 1998) used internal atomic states as a which-way detector in an atom interferometer, measured D and V independently, found D^2 + V^2 <= 1, and argued that the loss of visibility comes from the entanglement with the detector rather than from a momentum kick.

title: The quantum Zeno effect
establishes: Measuring the projector onto the initial state N times at equal intervals during a time t, with N >= Delta H t/hbar, gives survival probability at least (1 - (Delta H)^2 t^2/(hbar^2 N^2))^N, from |<e^{-iH tau/hbar}>| >= 1 - (Delta H tau/hbar)^2/2 by 1 - cos x <= x^2/2, and this tends to 1 as N grows by Bernoulli's inequality; under Rabi driving the probability that all N outcomes report survival is cos^(2N)(Omega t/2N) exactly.

title: Experiment: the Zeno effect in trapped ions
establishes: Itano, Heinzen, Bollinger and Wineland (1990) drove a pi pulse on a transition in about 5000 Be+ ions while probing the level population n = 1, 2, 4, ..., 64 times by short laser pulses, and the measured 1->2 transition probability matched the prediction (1 - cos^n(pi/n))/2 of the previous session, which holds because each measurement removes the transverse Bloch components and multiplies the z-component by cos(pi/n).

title: Quantum non-demolition measurement
establishes: If A is nondegenerate and commutes with the system Hamiltonian and the coupling, then the total evolution is U = sum_k P_k (x) V_k, A's distribution is unchanged, every observable commuting with A is undisturbed, and if the readout is precise, repeated readouts with fresh probes agree; a dispersive coupling Z (x) Z_probe is an example.

title: The Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem
establishes: If a measurement model conserves L_S (x) I + I (x) L_P, that is U^dagger L U = L, and measures A precisely and repeatably, so that U(phi (x) xi) lies in P_k H (x) Q_k K for every phi in the k-th eigenspace P_k H of A, with Q_k the pointer projectors, then <phi_i|L_S|phi_j> = 0 for eigenvectors of different eigenvalues, because both sides of <phi_i (x) xi|L|phi_j (x) xi> = <U(phi_i (x) xi)|L|U(phi_j (x) xi)> vanish term by term, and so [A, L_S] = 0: an observable that does not commute with an additive conserved quantity has no precise repeatable measurement model respecting the conservation law (Wigner 1952; Araki-Yanase 1960).
gap: Omitted: the approximate measurements whose error falls as the probe's spread of L_P grows, and Ozawa's quantitative error bound under the Yanase condition [M, L_P] = 0. Why: neither is used later. Where: H. Araki, M. M. Yanase, Phys. Rev. 120, 622 (1960); M. Ozawa, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88, 050402 (2002); L. Loveridge, P. Busch, Eur. Phys. J. D 62, 297 (2011).
note: Follow Loveridge and Busch (2011), Sec. 2. Left side: <phi_i|L_S|phi_j> + <phi_i|phi_j><xi|L_P|xi>, the second term zero. Right side: the L_S term has Q_i Q_j = 0 on the probe, the L_P term has P_i P_j = 0 on the system.

title: Weak measurement with a qubit pointer
establishes: For the coupling exp(-i g A (x) Y) with the pointer prepared in |0> and read in X, the pointer mean is <psi|sin(2gA)|psi> = 2g<A> + O(g^3), while the averaged system state changes at order g^2 and the state conditioned on one readout at order g, so A's mean is estimated with little disturbance from many runs.

title: Post-selection and weak values
establishes: Conditioning a weak measurement of A on a later projective outcome phi gives mean pointer readout 2g Re A_w + O(g^3 ||A||^3/|<phi|psi>|^3), valid when g||A|| << |<phi|psi>|, with A_w = <phi|A|psi>/<phi|psi>, which can lie outside the spectrum of A when <phi|psi> is small.

title: What a weak value is and is not
establishes: A weak value is a conditional average of pointer shifts in the regime g||A|| << |<phi|psi>| of the previous session, not an eigenvalue or a property held between preparation and post-selection; |A_w| <= ||A||/|<phi|psi>|, so a weak value far outside the spectrum requires a post-selection of probability at most ||A||^2/|A_w|^2; the 2008 spin-Hall and 2011 photon-trajectory experiments are read in these terms.

title: Joint measurability
establishes: Two POVMs are jointly measurable if they are the marginals of one POVM; an effect G with G <= P for a projector P satisfies G = PG = GP, hence two projective measurements are jointly measurable iff they commute; and non-commuting POVMs can be jointly measurable.

title: Joint measurability of unsharp qubit observables I: a joint POVM
establishes: For unit vectors a, b and 0 <= s_1, s_2 <= 1, the observables (I +- s_1 a.sigma)/2 and (I +- s_2 b.sigma)/2 have a joint POVM when |s_1 a + s_2 b| + |s_1 a - s_2 b| <= 2, constructed explicitly with four effects; for orthogonal a and b the condition is s_1^2 + s_2^2 <= 1.

title: Joint measurability of unsharp qubit observables II: necessity
establishes: Every joint POVM of these observables forces |s_1 a + s_2 b| + |s_1 a - s_2 b| <= 2, by writing its four effects in the Pauli basis, using positivity of each 2x2 effect and the triangle inequality.

title: Error and disturbance in a measurement model
establishes: For a measurement model (probe state, unitary U, pointer observable M), Ozawa's noise epsilon(A) is the root-mean-square of the noise operator N = U^dagger (I (x) M) U - A (x) I and the disturbance eta(B) that of D = U^dagger (B (x) I) U - B (x) I, both in the initial state, and epsilon(A) = 0 for every state iff the POVM the model induces on the system equals the spectral projectors of A.

title: The naive error-disturbance relation fails
establishes: A precise projective measurement of Z on a qubit has epsilon(Z) = 0 and finite eta(X), so the product bound epsilon(A) eta(B) >= (1/2)|<[A,B]>| fails on every state with <Y> nonzero, and Heisenberg's error-disturbance product bound is not a theorem.

title: The commutator identity for noise and disturbance operators
establishes: The noise and disturbance operators of a measurement model satisfy [N,D] + [N, B (x) I] + [A (x) I, D] = -[A,B] (x) I, because the evolved pointer observable commutes with the evolved system observable B.

title: Ozawa's error-disturbance inequality
establishes: Every measurement model satisfies epsilon(A) eta(B) + epsilon(A) Delta B + Delta A eta(B) >= (1/2)|<psi|[A,B]|psi>|, by taking the expectation of the identity and bounding each commutator term by the Robertson argument.

title: Experiment: tests of Ozawa's relation with neutron spins and photons
establishes: The neutron-spin experiment of Erhart et al. (2012) and the photon-polarisation experiment of Rozema et al. (2012) measured error and disturbance for tunable qubit measurements, by the three-state method and by weak measurement, and found the naive product bound violated and Ozawa's bound satisfied.

title: A state-independent error-disturbance relation for qubits
establishes: If error is measured as the worst-case total-variation distance between the outcome distributions of the target and the approximating observable over all input states, then any joint measurement whose marginals are (I +- s_1 sigma_x)/2 and (I +- s_2 sigma_z)/2 has errors e_x, e_z with (1 - 2 e_x)^2 + (1 - 2 e_z)^2 <= 1; for the Luders instrument of (I +- s sigma_x)/2 followed by a sharp sigma_z measurement, the second marginal is (I +- sqrt(1-s^2) sigma_z)/2, so the bound is attained and trades error against disturbance for this family.
gap: Omitted: the relation for arbitrary approximating observables with its optimal constants, and the Busch-Lahti-Werner position-momentum relation. Why: the first is a long optimisation over all joint measurements; the second needs Wasserstein distances on R and measure theory. Where: P. Busch, P. Lahti, R. F. Werner, Phys. Rev. A 89, 012129 (2014) and Rev. Mod. Phys. 86, 1261 (2014).

title: State-dependent and state-independent error-disturbance relations
establishes: Ozawa's relation bounds root-mean-square quantities in a given state, while the Busch-Lahti-Werner relation bounds worst-case distances over all states, so the two answer different questions and do not contradict each other.

title: Repeated measurement as Bayesian filtering of the density operator
establishes: Alternating unitary steps and instruments gives the recursion rho_{n+1} = Phi_{k_n}(U rho_n U^dagger)/tr(Phi_{k_n}(U rho_n U^dagger)), its average over outcomes is the composed channel, and it reduces to the classical Bayes filter of a hidden Markov model when all operators are diagonal in one basis.

title: Repeated weak measurement drives the state to an eigenstate
establishes: Under repeated unsharp Z measurement with Kraus operators sqrt((I +- s Z)/2) and no other dynamics, the population p_n of |0> is a martingale and E[sqrt(p_n(1 - p_n))] = (1 - s^2)^(n/2) sqrt(p_0(1 - p_0)), so for every delta > 0, P(p_n > 1 - delta) -> p_0 and P(p_n < delta) -> 1 - p_0 as n -> infinity (by Markov's inequality and E p_n = p_0), as the Born rule requires.

title: Measurement-based feedback in discrete time
establishes: Measuring with Kraus operators M_k and applying a unitary U_k chosen by the outcome gives the channel with Kraus operators U_k M_k, so feedback can prepare a target state from any input (for example |0>, by measuring Z and flipping on outcome 1), and on average it realises a channel and nothing beyond one.

title: Feedback stabilisation of a qubit under noise
establishes: With bit-flip noise of probability q per step, an unsharp Z measurement of strength s and an X flip applied on outcome -, the averaged population of |0> after each feedback step is exactly (1 + s)/2 whatever the state before it, so the loop holds the qubit near |0> with a deficit computed in closed form in s and q.

title: Excursion: the continuous-time limit of weak monitoring
establishes: Letting the measurement strength per step scale with the square root of the time step dt as dt -> 0 turns the quantum filter, formally, into a stochastic master equation driven by a Wiener process, whose average over records is a Lindblad equation.
gap: Omitted: the stochastic calculus (Ito integrals, the Wiener process) needed to state the limit, and the proof that the discrete filter converges to it. Why: it is beyond the book's finite, discrete probability. Where: H. M. Wiseman, G. J. Milburn, Quantum Measurement and Control (2010), Chs 3-5; K. Jacobs, D. A. Steck, Contemp. Phys. 47, 279 (2006); C. Pellegrini, Ann. Probab. 36, 2332 (2008).

title: Macrorealism and the Leggett-Garg inequality
establishes: If a +-1 quantity has a definite value at all times (macrorealism per se) and can be measured without affecting its later values (non-invasive measurability), its two-time correlations satisfy K = C_12 + C_23 - C_13 <= 1.

title: Leggett-Garg violation by a precessing qubit
establishes: For H = (hbar omega/2) X, with projective Z measurements at three times spaced by tau, K = 2 cos(omega tau) - cos(2 omega tau) for every initial state, with maximum 3/2 at omega tau = pi/3.

title: The clumsiness loophole
establishes: A Leggett-Garg violation can always be attributed to invasive measurement rather than to a failure of macrorealism, and ideal negative measurements and control experiments that measure the invasiveness (Knee et al. 2012; Wilde and Mizel 2012) narrow but do not close this loophole from inside the theory.

title: Experiment: Leggett-Garg tests with weak and ideal negative measurements
establishes: Palacios-Laloy et al. (2010) violated a Leggett-Garg inequality in a superconducting qubit using weak continuous measurement, and Knee et al. (2012) did so with ideal negative measurements on donor spins in silicon, each addressing invasiveness in a different way.

title: Q1 restated: observing and acting at once
establishes: Within the formalism every measurement is an instrument whose outcome and back-action come from one interaction, and Q1 splits into precise questions (joint measurability, error-disturbance relations, information-disturbance, QND, conservation-law limits (Wigner-Araki-Yanase), feedback as a channel), each answered in this Part with its assumptions.

title: Problems for Part XIX
establishes: Integrated problems on measurement models, weak values, error-disturbance bounds, filtering and feedback for qubits, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Hidden variables and Bell's theorem (Q3)
goal: State EPR and the ontological-model framework, derive local causality and its parts, prove Bell's and the CHSH inequalities with Fine's theorem, bound the quantum and no-signalling values, and give an entangled state with a local model.

title: Events, light cones and spacelike separation
establishes: Events are points (t, x) of spacetime; two events are spacelike separated when |x - x'| > c|t - t'|; the past light cone of an event is the set of events from which a signal no faster than light can reach it; and relativistic causality forbids any influence between spacelike-separated events.
note: Cited by local-causality for the common past of two measurements.

title: The EPR argument in Bohm's spin version
establishes: From the reality criterion, locality and the singlet's perfect anticorrelations, EPR infer that the spin components along every axis have predetermined values, which no quantum state assigns, so they conclude that the quantum description is incomplete.

title: Bohr's reply to EPR
establishes: Bohr rejected the phrase 'without in any way disturbing' in the reality criterion as ambiguous when the experimental arrangement defines the conditions of the prediction, which denies a premise rather than finding an error in the deduction.

title: Ontological models
establishes: An ontological model assigns to each preparation a distribution mu(lambda) over ontic states and to each measurement response probabilities xi(k|lambda) that reproduce the quantum probabilities, and it is psi-complete, psi-supplemented or psi-epistemic according to how mu relates to psi (Harrigan-Spekkens).
gap: Omitted: ontic state spaces other than finite or countable sets and intervals with a density. Why: general spaces need measure theory; the book proves its no-go theorems in these settings, and every proof given extends verbatim with sums replaced by integrals. Where: N. Harrigan, R. W. Spekkens, Found. Phys. 40, 125 (2010); M. S. Leifer, Quanta 3, 67 (2014).

title: Bell scenarios and behaviours
establishes: A bipartite Bell scenario is described by a behaviour p(ab|xy), which is no-signalling if each party's marginal does not depend on the other's setting; a quantum behaviour is p(ab|xy) = tr(rho (E_a|x (x) F_b|y)) for POVMs E_.|x, F_.|y, and every quantum behaviour is no-signalling.

title: Local causality as factorisation
establishes: Bell's local causality, applied to a variable lambda that includes everything relevant to the outcomes in the common past (the intersection of the two past light cones) of two spacelike-separated measurements, gives p(ab|xy,lambda) = p(a|x,lambda) p(b|y,lambda), and for n parties the product of the n single-party factors p(a_i|x_i,lambda).

title: Factorisation is parameter independence plus outcome independence
establishes: p(ab|xy,lambda) factorises iff p(a|xy,lambda) does not depend on y and symmetrically (parameter independence) and a and b are conditionally independent given x, y and lambda (outcome independence).

title: Measurement independence
establishes: A local model also assumes that the distribution of lambda does not depend on the settings, p(lambda|xy) = p(lambda), an assumption logically separate from factorisation.

title: Perfect anticorrelation and factorisation imply determinism
establishes: In a factorisable, measurement-independent model, perfect anticorrelation for equal settings forces each outcome to be a deterministic function of lambda and the local setting.

title: Bell's 1964 theorem
establishes: Every factorisable, measurement-independent model reproducing the singlet's perfect anticorrelation satisfies |E(a,b) - E(a,c)| <= 1 + E(b,c), and the singlet violates this for coplanar a, b, c at 0, 60 and 120 degrees.

title: Mermin's three-setting device
establishes: With three settings per side, chosen independently and uniformly, and instruction sets fixed at the source, the lights agree in at least 5/9 of runs, whereas the singlet measured along directions 120 degrees apart, with agreement read as opposite spins, agrees in 1/2 of runs and always for equal settings.

title: Every local model is a mixture of local deterministic strategies
establishes: For any finite number of parties, a behaviour has a factorisable, measurement-independent model iff it is a convex combination of the finitely many deterministic behaviours prod_i [a_i = f_i(x_i)].

title: The local polytope
establishes: The local behaviours of a finite scenario with any number of parties form a polytope whose vertices are the deterministic strategies, so a linear Bell inequality holds for all local models iff it holds at every vertex.

title: The CHSH inequality
establishes: For two settings and +-1 outcomes per side, every local behaviour satisfies |E00 + E01 + E10 - E11| <= 2 and the three forms obtained by moving the minus sign to another term, eight linear inequalities in all, checked on the 16 deterministic vertices, and the bound 2 is attained.

title: Fine's theorem I: local models and joint distributions
establishes: A behaviour of the CHSH scenario has a local model iff some joint distribution of four +-1 variables A0, A1, B0, B1 has the observed pair distributions p(a,b|x,y) as its marginals.

title: Fine's theorem II: joint distributions of three +-1 variables
establishes: Given consistent, nonnegative pair distributions for (X,Y), (X,Z) and (Y,Z) of +-1 variables, a joint distribution exists iff 1 + s1s2 C_XY + s2s3 C_YZ + s1s3 C_XZ >= 0 for all signs, with the triple moment as the one free parameter; given only (X,Y) and (X,Z), the conditionally independent gluing p(x)p(y|x)p(z|x) always gives one.
note: Follow Fine (PRL 48, 291; J. Math. Phys. 23, 1306, 1982) and Halliwell, Phys. Lett. A 378, 2945 (2014), Sec. IV: each sign pattern s and its negation bound the triple moment to an interval of length 2(1 + pair terms); pair positivity makes the intervals meet.

title: Fine's theorem III: sufficiency of CHSH in general
establishes: A no-signalling CHSH behaviour has a joint distribution iff some value of C_B0B1 is admissible at once for the (B0,B1) pair and for the triples (A0,B0,B1) and (A1,B0,B1), the two triples then being glued as p(a0|b0b1)p(a1|b0b1)q(b0b1); since each triple is admissible on its own, the one-dimensional intersection of intervals leaves only |E00+E01| + |E10-E11| <= 2 and |E00-E01| + |E10+E11| <= 2, the eight CHSH inequalities, so positivity, no-signalling and the CHSH inequalities describe the local polytope completely.
note: Follow Fine (1982). Triple (A0,B0,B1) gives C_B0B1 in [|E00+E01|-1, 1-|E00-E01|], similarly for A1; each meets the (B0,B1) pair-positivity interval because the gluing of fine-triples always exists; Helly in one dimension finishes. Cite Halliwell (2014) only for the zero-average case, whose explicit construction goes to the problems.

title: The set of quantum behaviours
establishes: Behaviours tr(rho (E_a|x (x) F_b|y)) form a convex set containing the local polytope, and without loss of generality the state may be taken pure and the measurements projective, by purification and Naimark dilation.

title: The no-signalling polytope
establishes: The behaviours satisfying positivity, normalisation and no-signalling form a closed bounded set cut out by finitely many linear constraints; each of its extreme points is the unique solution of its tight constraints, so there are finitely many, and by Minkowski's theorem the set is their convex hull, a polytope, containing every quantum behaviour, which in turn contains every local behaviour.

title: The quantum CHSH value
establishes: With the singlet and spin measurements in one plane at a0 = 0, a1 = 90, b0 = 45 and b1 = -45 degrees, E00 + E01 + E10 - E11 = -2 sqrt2.

title: The square of the CHSH operator
establishes: For self-adjoint A_x, B_y with squares I acting on different factors, C = A0(B0 + B1) + A1(B0 - B1) satisfies C^2 = 4I - [A0,A1] (x) [B0,B1].

title: Tsirelson's bound
establishes: Every quantum behaviour, which by the reduction to projective measurements may be taken with A_x^2 = B_y^2 = I, has CHSH value at most 2 sqrt2, because ||[A0,A1]|| <= 2 and ||X (x) Y|| <= ||X|| ||Y|| give ||C^2|| <= 8 and hence |tr(rho C)| <= ||C|| <= 2 sqrt2, in every dimension.

title: A sum-of-squares proof of Tsirelson's bound and its equality conditions
establishes: 2 sqrt2 I - C = (1/sqrt2)[(A0 - (B0 + B1)/sqrt2)^2 + (A1 - (B0 - B1)/sqrt2)^2], so equality forces {A0,A1} to vanish on the support of rho_A and, by the mirrored decomposition, {B0,B1} on the support of rho_B.

title: Two-outcome observables and their extreme points
establishes: A two-outcome POVM {E, I - E} corresponds to the observable A = 2E - I with -I <= A <= I, these operators form a convex set whose extreme points are exactly the self-adjoint A with A^2 = I, and a function affine in each of several such operators separately attains its maximum when every one is extreme.

title: The CHSH value of two-qubit Werner states
establishes: Over all two-outcome measurements on each qubit, the Werner state p|Psi-><Psi-| + (1-p)I/4 has maximal CHSH value max(2, 2 sqrt2 p): by the extreme-point reduction each observable is +-I or m.sigma; with any +-I the value is at most 2, and with spin observables it is p(|b0+b1| + |b0-b1|) <= 2 sqrt2 p. So it violates CHSH iff p > 1/sqrt2, although it is entangled for every p > 1/3.
note: With A0 = +-I, condition on Alice's A1 outcome a1: the CHSH operator on Bob's side becomes +-(B0+B1) + a1(B0-B1), which is 2B0 or 2B1 up to sign, of norm at most 2; likewise for the other cases. The spin bound is the parallelogram law; it is attained by the angles of chsh-quantum-value at p = 1.

title: A local model for Werner states with p <= 1/2
establishes: For projective measurements, the Werner state with p <= 1/2 has a local model: with lambda uniform on the sphere, Alice outputs sgn(a.lambda) and Bob outputs -1 with probability (1 + b.lambda)/2 and +1 otherwise, which gives uniform marginals and correlation -E[sgn(a.lambda) b.lambda] = -(a.b)/2, the statistics of p = 1/2, and mixing with uniformly random local outputs gives every p < 1/2; so Werner states with 1/3 < p <= 1/2 are entangled yet admit a local model for projective measurements (the threshold 1/2 is Werner's, 1989).
gap: Omitted: local models for general POVMs (Barrett, p <= 5/12) and for projective measurements beyond p = 1/2, and the exact threshold, which is not known in closed form. Why: the models are longer constructions, and the larger thresholds rest on Grothendieck's constant or computer-assisted bounds; nothing later uses them. Where: R. F. Werner, Phys. Rev. A 40, 4277 (1989); J. Barrett, Phys. Rev. A 65, 042302 (2002); A. Acin, N. Gisin, B. Toner, Phys. Rev. A 73, 062105 (2006); R. Augusiak, M. Demianowicz, A. Acin, J. Phys. A 47, 424002 (2014).
note: Write b = (a.b)a + b_perp; E[sgn(a.lambda) b_perp.lambda] = 0 by the rotation by pi about a, and E|a.lambda| = 1/2. A qubit projective measurement is trivial (+-I) or a spin direction, and two-outcome statistics are fixed by marginals and correlation.

title: The Popescu-Rohrlich box
establishes: The behaviour with a XOR b = xy and uniform marginals is no-signalling, reaches CHSH value 4, is an extreme point of the no-signalling polytope, and is not quantum by Tsirelson's bound, so no-signalling alone does not single out quantum correlations.

title: The vertices of the CHSH no-signalling polytope
establishes: The no-signalling polytope of the two-setting, two-outcome scenario has exactly 24 vertices: the 16 local deterministic behaviours and the 8 PR boxes a XOR b = xy XOR alpha x XOR beta y XOR gamma (Barrett et al., Phys. Rev. A 71, 022101, 2005).
note: Follow Barrett et al. (2005), Sec. II.

title: Hardy's paradox
establishes: If p(0,1|0,1) = p(1,0|1,0) = p(0,0|1,1) = 0, every local deterministic strategy, and hence every local model, gives p(0,0|0,0) = 0, while a two-qubit pure state with unequal nonzero Schmidt coefficients and suitable spin measurements gives it positive probability.

title: Jordan's lemma for two +-1 observables
establishes: For self-adjoint A0, A1 with A0^2 = A1^2 = I, the space is an orthogonal direct sum of subspaces of dimension 1 or 2, each invariant under both, obtained from eigenvectors v of the unitary A0A1 as span{v, A0 v}.
note: If A0A1 v = lambda v, then A0 v is an eigenvector with eigenvalue conj(lambda), A1 v = lambda A0 v, and span{v, A0 v} is invariant under both; induct on the orthogonal complement, which is invariant since A0, A1 are self-adjoint. Rabelo, Zhi, Scarani, PRL 109, 180401 (2012), Lemma 1.

title: The maximal probability of Hardy's event
establishes: Over pure states and projective measurements satisfying Hardy's three zero conditions, the fourth probability is at most (5 sqrt5 - 11)/2, about 0.09: for two qubits by reducing to one variable and maximising, with this value attained, and in every finite dimension since by Jordan's lemma on each side the Hardy probability is a convex combination of block probabilities, each block satisfying the zero conditions, and blocks of dimension 1 give 0 by the previous Hardy session (Rabelo, Zhi, Scarani, Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 180401, 2012).

title: The GHZ argument
establishes: For the three-qubit GHZ state the products XXX, XYY, YXY, YYX have definite values +1, -1, -1, -1, which no assignment of predetermined +-1 values to X and Y on each qubit can reproduce, so every local deterministic strategy fails on at least one of the four setting choices and, with settings chosen uniformly, a local model errs in at least 1/4 of runs; the contradiction uses only outcomes predicted with certainty, not statistics.

title: Mermin's three-party inequality
establishes: Local models satisfy |<XXX> - <XYY> - <YXY> - <YYX>| <= 2, while the GHZ state gives 4, the algebraic maximum.

title: Problems for Part XX
establishes: Integrated problems on Bell inequalities, Fine's construction (including the explicit joint distribution built from the four correlators when all single-party marginals are uniform, after Halliwell 2014), quantum values and the no-signalling polytope, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Bell experiments, loopholes and measurement dependence (Q3)
goal: Treat Bell tests as hypothesis tests, compute the detection loophole exactly, state what each landmark experiment closed, quantify what giving up measurement independence costs, and show that classical causal explanations of a violation are fine-tuned.

title: Bell tests as hypothesis tests
establishes: If each trial's settings x_i, y_i are chosen uniformly and independently of everything earlier, including that trial's hidden variable, then for any local model, even one with memory of earlier trials, the win indicators W_i = [a_i b_i = (-1)^(x_i y_i)] satisfy E[W_i | past] = 1/2 + S_i/8 <= 3/4, where S_i <= 2 is the CHSH value of the trial's local behaviour given the past. Azuma-Hoeffding then gives P(sum_i W_i - 3n/4 >= t) <= exp(-2t^2/n), a p-value that does not assume independent or identically distributed trials.

title: The detection loophole: a local model under post-selection
establishes: For 2/3 <= eta <= 1, the following local model gives each side's detector probability eta at each setting, coincidences eta^2 and post-selected CHSH value 4/eta - 2: with weight 3eta^2 - 2eta, all four detectors fire and a deterministic strategy wins three CHSH pairs; with weight eta(1 - eta) each (four strategies), one party fires at only one setting while the other fires at both, winning both pairs that are counted; with weight (1 - eta)^2, nothing fires. The value is 2 sqrt2 at eta = 2(sqrt2 - 1), about 82.8%, and 4 at eta = 2/3, so post-selected violations need a fair-sampling assumption.

title: The post-selected CHSH bound for local models
establishes: Let eta be the minimum over settings i, j of P(A_i detects | B_j detects) and P(B_j detects | A_i detects). Every local model in which each detection is decided locally gives post-selected |S| <= 4/eta - 2 (Larsson 1998), proved on the detection sets of its deterministic strategies with the union bound, since a ratio of probabilities cannot be checked at vertices. This includes Garg and Mermin's case, where single efficiencies are eta and coincidences eta^2. If only the single efficiencies eta are fixed and detections may be correlated, coincidences can fall to 2eta - 1 and the bound becomes 2/(2eta - 1), which some model attains; so the model of detection-loophole-model is optimal under either of the first two definitions.

title: Counting non-detections: the efficiency threshold
establishes: Assigning +1 to every non-detection turns any local model into a local model with +-1 outcomes, so CHSH <= 2 holds with no fair-sampling assumption. The singlet strategy with independent detection efficiency eta on each side then gives 2 sqrt2 eta^2 + 2(1 - eta)^2, since the uniform marginals cancel the eta(1 - eta) cross terms, and this exceeds 2 iff eta > 2/(1 + sqrt2) = 2(sqrt2 - 1), about 82.8%.

title: The Clauser-Horne-Eberhard inequality
establishes: With outcomes {+, no-click} on each side, every local model satisfies the Clauser-Horne inequality p(++|00) + p(++|01) + p(++|10) - p(++|11) - p_A(+|0) - p_B(+|0) <= 0, checked on the deterministic vertices; it uses only detection counts, so it needs no fair sampling. With non-maximally entangled states (Eberhard), it is violated for every eta > 2/3 by suitable states and settings, the threshold tending to 2/3 as the state tends to a product state.
gap: Omitted: the optimisation over states and settings showing a violation for every eta > 2/3. Why: it is long (the optimum is a root of a quartic) and nothing later uses it. Where: P. H. Eberhard, Phys. Rev. A 47, R747 (1993); J.-A. Larsson, J. Semitecolos, Phys. Rev. A 63, 022117 (2001); J.-A. Larsson, J. Phys. A 47, 424003 (2014), Sec. 3.4, with the quartic of Lima et al. (2012) cited there.

title: The locality loophole and the experiments of Freedman-Clauser, Aspect and Weihs
establishes: Freedman and Clauser (1972) violated a Bell-type inequality with fixed polarisers, Aspect, Dalibard and Roger (1982) switched settings during photon flight with periodic switches, and Weihs et al. (1998) chose settings randomly with spacelike separation over 400 m, closing the locality loophole while leaving the detection loophole open.

title: The loophole-free Bell tests of 2015
establishes: Hensen et al. (Delft: electron spins 1.3 km apart linked by entanglement swapping, S = 2.42 +- 0.20, p = 0.039), Giustina et al. (Vienna) and Shalm et al. (NIST) (photons, Eberhard-type inequalities, high-efficiency detectors) closed the detection and locality loopholes together, with p-values computed without assuming independent trials.

title: The freedom-of-choice loophole and the cosmic and human-choice Bell tests
establishes: Measurement independence cannot be tested directly, and experiments push back the latest time at which settings and source could share a cause by choosing settings with light from Milky Way stars (Handsteiner et al. 2017, about 600 years), from distant quasars (Rauch et al. 2018, billions of years), or from human input (BIG Bell Test 2018), the cosmic tests assuming fair sampling.

title: Superdeterminism
establishes: If p(lambda|xy) may depend on the settings, a local deterministic model reproduces every behaviour, including the PR box and the singlet, so every Bell violation can be explained by correlations between hidden variables and settings, at the price of such a correlation for every method of choosing settings; read with lambda depending on future settings rather than on a common past, the same model is retrocausal, which differs from superdeterminism in causal story, not in correlation structure.

title: Quantitative relaxations of measurement independence
establishes: If the hidden-variable distributions for any two setting pairs are within total variation delta, every factorisable model has CHSH value at most 2 + 6 delta, and for delta <= 1/3 this is attained by four deterministic strategies s_xy, each losing only on pair xy, with p(s_xy|xy) = (1 - 3delta)/4 and the others (1 + delta)/4; so the quantum value 2 sqrt2 requires delta >= (sqrt2 - 1)/3.
gap: Omitted: Hall's model reproducing the singlet correlations with measurement-dependence capacity about 0.066 bits, and the information-theoretic (mutual-information) measures of Hall and of Barrett-Gisin. Why: the model is continuous on the sphere and its capacity is evaluated numerically, and relating the information measures to total variation needs Pinsker's inequality, which is not built here. Where: M. J. W. Hall, Phys. Rev. Lett. 105, 250404 (2010); M. J. W. Hall, Phys. Rev. A 84, 022102 (2011); J. Barrett, N. Gisin, Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 100406 (2011).

title: Classical causal explanations of Bell correlations are fine-tuned
establishes: In a classical causal model of a CHSH experiment that reproduces a violation, the influence the violation requires, whether from a setting to the distant outcome, from outcome to outcome, or from the settings to lambda, is nonzero at the level of lambda, since otherwise the CHSH inequality holds, yet it must cancel in the observed marginals, as no-signalling demands; so the observed independence of each outcome from the distant setting holds only by a tuning of the model's parameters, not by its causal structure (Wood-Spekkens 2015).
gap: Omitted: the general theorem over all causal structures on the observed and latent variables. Why: it needs the d-separation calculus and the faithfulness principle of causal discovery, which the book does not build; the session proves the three mechanisms that the earlier sessions consider. Where: C. J. Wood, R. W. Spekkens, New J. Phys. 17, 033002 (2015).
note: Define fine-tuning as an observed conditional independence that is not implied by the causal graph. For each mechanism, write the observed marginal as a sum over lambda and show the lambda-level dependence must be nonzero.

title: No extension of quantum theory predicts outcomes better
establishes: If each setting is free, in that it is uncorrelated with every variable outside its future light cone, then no additional variable available before the measurement predicts the outcomes of measurements on a maximally entangled pair better than the quantum state does (Colbeck-Renner 2011), so a local or nonlocal extension that respects free choice can add no checkable predictive content.
gap: Omitted: the proof, which uses the chained Bell inequalities with N settings and their quantum values as N -> infinity. Why: the chained inequalities are a separate sequence of calculations used nowhere else. Where: R. Colbeck, R. Renner, Nat. Commun. 2, 411 (2011); S. L. Braunstein, C. M. Caves, Ann. Phys. 202, 22 (1990).

title: What Bell's theorem assumes and what it does not
establishes: The CHSH theorem assumes local causality (parameter and outcome independence), measurement independence and single definite outcomes, and does not assume determinism, a particular hidden-variable space or anything about measurement disturbance; each surviving model gives up a named assumption.

title: Problems for Part XXI
establishes: Integrated problems on p-values, detection-efficiency models and measurement-dependent models, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Contextuality and the reality of the quantum state (Q3)
goal: Prove the Kochen-Specker theorem in every dimension at least three, Busch's and Gleason's theorems, KCBS and Spekkens contextuality and the link to computation, give a psi-epistemic qubit model, prove the PBR theorem, and restate Q3.

title: Noncontextual value assignments
establishes: A noncontextual value assignment gives each observable a value in its spectrum and respects functional relations among commuting observables; equivalently it assigns 0 or 1 to every projector so that exactly one projector in each orthonormal basis (each context) receives 1, which turns its existence into a colouring problem, and since commuting observables are functions of one common observable, v(A + B) = v(A) + v(B) and v(AB) = v(A)v(B) for commuting A, B.

title: Von Neumann's no-go theorem and its additivity assumption
establishes: No dispersion-free assignment can make values additive for non-commuting observables, since sigma_x + sigma_z has eigenvalues +-sqrt2 while the values of sigma_x and sigma_z are +-1, so von Neumann's assumption of additivity for all observables excludes hidden variables by fiat, as Hermann (1935) and Bell (1966) observed.

title: Bell's 1966 hidden-variable model for a qubit
establishes: For a qubit with Bloch vector n, a hidden variable lambda uniform on [-1/2, 1/2] and the rule 'sigma.m takes the value s(m) if lambda + |n.m|/2 > 0 and -s(m) otherwise' reproduce the probabilities (1 + n.m)/2, where s(m) = sign(n.m) when n.m != 0 and, for m perpendicular to n, s(m) is the sign of the first nonzero component of m along a fixed orthonormal pair e1, e2 of the plane perpendicular to n (Bell's tie-break). Because s(-m) = -s(m), the rule assigns opposite values to m and -m, and it is noncontextual because in dimension 2 each projector lies in only one basis.

title: The Peres-Mermin square
establishes: Nine two-qubit Pauli products arranged in a 3x3 grid have mutually commuting rows and columns whose products are +I except one column with product -I, so no noncontextual assignment of +-1 values exists in dimension 4, whatever the state.

title: The magic-square game
establishes: In the magic-square game classical players win with probability at most 8/9, while players who share two Bell pairs and measure the Peres-Mermin observables win with probability 1, which turns the Peres-Mermin square into a Bell-type test.

title: The 18-vector Kochen-Specker set in dimension four
establishes: Eighteen vectors of R^4 forming nine orthogonal bases, each vector in exactly two of them, admit no 0-1 assignment with one 1 per basis, because the number of 1s would be both odd (nine bases) and even (each vector counted twice).

title: Peres' 33 rays in dimension three
establishes: Peres' 33 rays are the images under coordinate permutations and sign changes of (0,0,1), (0,1,1), (0,1,sqrt2) and (1,1,sqrt2), giving 3 + 6 + 12 + 12 rays. They contain 72 orthogonal pairs: 48 lie in 16 orthogonal triples and 24 do not. The set is invariant under the 48 signed permutations, so a colouring may be assumed to give 1 to (0,0,1), and then, using x -> -x and y -> -y, which fix (0,0,1), also to (1,0,1) and (0,1,1).

title: The Kochen-Specker theorem in dimension three
establishes: No assignment of 0 and 1 to Peres' 33 rays gives exactly one 1 in each of the 16 orthogonal triples and at most one 1 in each of the 72 orthogonal pairs (a noncontextual assignment must do both, since every orthogonal pair completes to a basis); after the choices (0,0,1) = (1,0,1) = (0,1,1) = 1 allowed by symmetry, forced deductions reach a contradiction.

title: The Kochen-Specker theorem in every dimension at least three
establishes: Place a copy of Peres' set in span(e_i, e_j, e_k) for every 3-subset of {1, ..., d}, and complete each of its triples, and the third vector of each of its orthogonal pairs, with the remaining e_l. The standard basis is one of the completed bases, so a colouring gives 1 to exactly one e_m; on a 3-subset containing m every completing e_l is 0, so that copy would need a Peres colouring, which is impossible. This gives a finite Kochen-Specker set in every d >= 3, so no noncontextual value assignment exists there, while in d = 2 Bell's model gives one.

title: Frame functions and the statement of Gleason's theorem
establishes: A frame function assigns nonnegative weights to unit vectors with a constant sum over every orthonormal basis, every density operator gives one by v -> <v|rho|v>, and in dimension 2 there are frame functions of no such form.

title: Generalised probability measures on effects
establishes: A function v on effects with v(I) = 1, v >= 0 and v(E + F) = v(E) + v(F) whenever E + F <= I is monotone and satisfies v(qE) = q v(E) for every rational q in [0,1]; an effect appearing in several POVMs gets one value (noncontextuality for effects), and since v(I/2) + v(I/2) = v(I) = 1, no 0-1-valued such v exists, even for a qubit, which excludes only models that are outcome-deterministic for unsharp measurements.

title: Busch's theorem I: extension to a linear functional
establishes: Monotonicity upgrades rational to real homogeneity, so v is additive and positively homogeneous on effects, and it then extends uniquely to a real-linear functional on the self-adjoint operators by the extension step of affine-extension-lemma, each self-adjoint operator being a difference of positive multiples of effects.

title: Busch's theorem II: the Born rule for effects
establishes: Every generalised probability measure on effects is v(E) = tr(rho E) for a unique density operator rho, in every dimension including 2.

title: Frame functions on the sphere S^2
establishes: A signed frame function of weight W on S^2 is a real function with f(a) + f(b) + f(c) = W for every orthonormal basis; nonnegative frame functions are signed ones, f + c has weight W + 3c, and real linear combinations of signed frame functions are signed frame functions. For every signed frame function f: f(x) = f(-x); f(a) + f(a') = W - f(n) for orthogonal a, a' on the great circle with pole n; and f(s) + f(Rs) = W - f(p) is constant on the equator E_p, where R is the quarter turn about p.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition.  An independent full proof: A. Dvurecenskij, Gleason's Theorem and Its Applications (Kluwer, 1993), Ch. 3.

title: A functional equation on [0,1]
establishes: Let D be a countable subset of (0,1) and g: [0,1] minus D -> R nondecreasing, with g(0) = 0 and g(a) + g(b) + g(c) = 1 whenever a + b + c = 1 and a, b, c lie outside D. Then g(a) = a for every a outside D.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition.

title: Frame functions do not rise along descending circles
establishes: Let f be a frame function on S^2 that is constant on E_p with f(p) > sup f - eps. For s != p in the northern hemisphere about p, let C(s) be the great circle through s and the point p x s of E_p, so that s is its highest point. Then f(t) < f(s) + eps for every t on C(s).
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition. Proof: with t' on C(s) orthogonal to t, f(t) + f(t') = f(s) + c, and a frame through t' and a point of E_p gives f(t') > c - eps.

title: Piron's lemma: reaching lower points by descending circles
establishes: If s and t lie in the open northern hemisphere about p and t is strictly lower than s, then t is reached from s in finitely many steps, each moving from a point x to a point of the great circle C(x) through x and p x x (for x = p, any great circle through p).
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition. Use the corrected version of this lemma.

title: Gleason in R^3: the symmetric case
establishes: A bounded signed frame function on S^2 that attains its maximum at p and is constant, equal to c, on E_p is f(x) = c + (f(p) - c)<x,p>^2: by the slope lemma and Piron's lemma f does not increase as latitude decreases, so it depends on <x,p>^2 except at countably many latitudes, and the functional equation fixes it.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition.

title: Nonnegative frame functions attain their extremes
establishes: A nonnegative frame function on S^2 attains its supremum and its infimum, and hence so does every bounded signed frame function, by adding a constant.
gap: Omitted: the existence of a frame function with values in [m,M] that agrees, on a given countable set, with the pointwise limit of a sequence of [m,M]-valued frame functions. Why: the proof uses compactness of [m,M]^{S^2} (Tychonoff's theorem for an uncountable product), which the book does not build. Where: the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (2018), Lemma 7; J. R. Munkres, Topology, 2nd ed., Thm 37.3.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition. CKM's topological argument here is wrong; follow the thesis's corrected Proposition 2.

title: Gleason's theorem in R^3
establishes: Every nonnegative frame function on the unit sphere of R^3 is x -> <x,Ax> for a symmetric matrix A.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition. The thesis's Lemma 8 (assembly).

title: From R^3 to R^d and C^d
establishes: For d >= 3, every nonnegative frame function on the unit sphere of R^d or C^d is v -> <v,Av> for a self-adjoint A: it is quadratic on each real subspace spanned by three orthonormal vectors, hence a Hermitian form on each two-dimensional complex subspace, and these forms agree on overlaps and assemble into A.
note: Follow the corrected Cooke-Keane-Moran proof in the Chalmers thesis 'Gleasons sats' (odr.chalmers.se/handle/20.500.12380/257144), not CKM's original, which has an oversight in Piron's lemma and an erroneous topological step in the extreme-value proposition. The thesis's Lemmas 9-12.

title: Gleason's theorem for projectors
establishes: In every dimension d >= 3, a function v on projectors with v >= 0, v(I) = 1 and v(P + Q) = v(P) + v(Q) for orthogonal P, Q is v(P) = tr(rho P) for a unique density operator rho, since x -> v(|x><x|) is a nonnegative frame function; so in d >= 3 it reaches Busch's conclusion on projectors from additivity on orthogonal projectors alone, and it fails in d = 2.

title: Kochen-Specker from Gleason's theorem
establishes: Given Gleason's theorem, a 0-1 noncontextual assignment on C^3 would be the continuous function v -> <v|rho|v> on the unit sphere, which takes only the values 0 and 1 and so is constant along every great circle by the intermediate value theorem, contradicting one 1 per basis; this is a second route to the result proved directly by Peres' rays.

title: Bell nonlocality as contextuality in spacelike-separated contexts
establishes: A noncontextual model for measurements grouped into contexts is a probability distribution over noncontextual value assignments, equivalently a joint distribution of all the measurements whose marginals on each context match the data. For a Bell scenario with contexts {A_x, B_y} these assignments are the deterministic local strategies, so a behaviour has a local model iff it has a noncontextual model, and Bell inequalities are noncontextuality inequalities whose compatibility is guaranteed by spacelike separation.

title: The KCBS inequality
establishes: For five projectors in which cyclically adjacent pairs are orthogonal, every noncontextual model gives sum_i p(P_i = 1) <= 2, because the largest set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices of a pentagon has two elements.

title: The quantum violation of the KCBS inequality
establishes: Five unit vectors in R^3 forming a pentagram about a symmetry axis, with the state along that axis, give sum_i p_i = sqrt5 > 2.

title: The quantum KCBS value is at most sqrt5
establishes: For any state and any projectors P_1, ..., P_5 with P_i P_{i+1} = 0 (indices mod 5), sum_i tr(rho P_i) <= sqrt5: for pure psi, let v_i = P_i psi/||P_i psi|| (skip i when P_i psi = 0) and w_i = u_{2i mod 5}, the KCBS vectors; the v_i (x) w_i are orthonormal, and Bessel's inequality against psi (x) c gives sum_i p_i/sqrt5 <= 1; mixed states follow by convexity (Lovasz 1979, no duality needed).

title: Experiment: tests of contextuality and the compatibility loophole
establishes: Kirchmair et al. (2009, trapped ions, Peres-Mermin square) and Lapkiewicz et al. (2011, photonic qutrits, KCBS) measured contextuality witnesses beyond their noncontextual bounds, with conclusions that depend on how well the compatibility and sharpness of the measurements were verified.

title: Operational equivalence and Spekkens noncontextuality
establishes: Preparations (or measurements) that give identical statistics for all measurements (or on all preparations) are operationally equivalent, an ontological model is preparation (or measurement) noncontextual if it represents equivalent ones identically, and measurement noncontextuality with outcome determinism for sharp measurements is Kochen-Specker noncontextuality.

title: Preparation contextuality of the qubit
establishes: For six qubit states a, A, b, B, c, C forming three antipodal pairs at 120 degrees in a plane, the five decompositions I/2 = (a+A)/2 = (b+B)/2 = (c+C)/2 = (a+b+c)/3 = (A+B+C)/3 are operationally equivalent, and no preparation-noncontextual model reproduces the six states' statistics for the three antipodal measurements (Spekkens 2005).

title: Computing OR from GHZ correlations with parity side-processing
establishes: Measuring each GHZ qubit in X or Y according to linear functions of two input bits and adding the outcomes mod 2 computes the OR of the inputs deterministically, a nonlinear function that mod-2 linear side-processing alone cannot compute (Anders and Browne 2009).

title: Nonlinear measurement-based computation requires contextuality
establishes: If a measurement-based computation with mod-2 linear side-processing computes a nonlinear Boolean function deterministically, its measurement statistics admit no noncontextual value assignment (Raussendorf 2013).

title: Contextuality and magic-state computation
establishes: For qudits of odd prime dimension, Howard, Wallman, Veitch and Emerson (2014) showed that a state enables universal computation by state injection only if it violates a noncontextuality inequality built from stabilizer measurements; the session states this informally and relates it to Raussendorf's theorem.
gap: Omitted: the definitions of qudit stabilizer operations and state injection, and the proof, which uses the discrete Wigner function and the stabilizer formalism. Why: neither is developed here. Where: M. Howard, J. Wallman, V. Veitch, J. Emerson, Nature 510, 351 (2014), with Supplementary Information.

title: Overlapping ontic distributions and preparation independence
establishes: A model is psi-epistemic iff some two distinct pure states have overlapping ontic distributions, and preparation independence says that independently prepared systems have product ontic distributions.

title: The Kochen-Specker qubit model: a psi-epistemic example
establishes: With lambda a unit vector of R^3, preparing the qubit state with Bloch vector n by sampling lambda with density 4 max(n.lambda, 0) relative to the uniform distribution, and letting the projective measurement along m give + iff m.lambda > 0, reproduces P(+|n,m) = (1 + n.m)/2; the hemispheres of two distinct non-orthogonal states overlap, so the model is psi-epistemic (Kochen-Specker 1967).
note: By rotation invariance take n = e_z and m = (sin t, 0, cos t); the probability is a double integral in (z, phi) computed in closed form. Non-orthogonal means n != -n'.

title: The PBR theorem for |0> and |+>
establishes: Under preparation independence, a two-qubit entangled measurement whose four outcomes are each orthogonal to one of |00>, |0+>, |+0>, |++> shows that the ontic distributions of |0> and |+> cannot overlap.

title: The two-copy PBR measurement for distant enough pairs of states
establishes: Writing two pure states as cos(theta/2)|0> +- sin(theta/2)|1>, a phase-adjusted entangled measurement on two copies has each outcome orthogonal to one product preparation whenever |<psi0|psi1>| = cos theta <= 1/sqrt2, so their ontic distributions cannot overlap.

title: The n-copy PBR measurement
establishes: For two pure states cos(theta/2)|0> +- sin(theta/2)|1> with 0 < theta <= pi/2 and n with 2^(1/n) - 1 <= tan(theta/2), there are alpha, beta such that applying Z_beta to each qubit, then R_alpha (the phase e^{i alpha} on |0...0>), then H to each qubit, and measuring in the computational basis, gives 2^n outcomes each orthogonal to one product preparation; beta exists by the intermediate value theorem applied to |f(beta)|, with f(beta) = 1 - (1 + e^{i beta} tan(theta/2))^n, f(0) <= -1 and 0 <= f(pi) <= 1, and then e^{i alpha} = f(beta).

title: The PBR theorem for any two distinct pure states
establishes: Any two distinct pure states can be written, after a choice of basis and phases, as cos(theta/2)|0> +- sin(theta/2)|1> with 0 < theta <= pi/2, and by Bernoulli's inequality n >= 1/tan(theta/2) copies satisfy 2^(1/n) - 1 <= tan(theta/2); so the n-copy measurement excludes overlap of their ontic distributions, and every preparation-independent ontological model that reproduces quantum predictions is psi-ontic.

title: What the PBR theorem assumes
establishes: PBR relies on the ontological-models framework and on preparation independence, and psi-epistemic models survive only by dropping one of them, as in retrocausal or relational accounts.

title: Q3 restated: local realism that no experiment can check
establishes: Q3 splits into precise statements, each with its assumptions: local models with measurement independence are excluded at a computed p-value by loophole-free data; measurement-dependent and retrocausal local models reproduce every behaviour at a quantified cost in measurement dependence, and every classical causal account of a violation is fine-tuned, so the influence it posits shows in no observed statistic; no extension respecting free choice predicts better than quantum theory; entanglement alone does not exclude a local model; macrorealism survives through the clumsiness loophole; and noncontextual and psi-epistemic models are excluded under named assumptions, while a psi-epistemic qubit model exists.

title: Problems for Part XXII
establishes: Integrated problems on colourings and parity proofs, noncontextuality inequalities and their quantum values, Busch's theorem and the PBR measurements, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: The measurement problem and decoherence (Q2)
goal: State the measurement problem through the von Neumann chain, the insolubility theorem, the movable cut and Maudlin's trilemma, then derive what decoherence does, which states it selects, how records spread, and what it leaves open.

title: The von Neumann chain
establishes: Composing pre-measurement unitaries system -> apparatus -> environment -> observer yields sum_k c_k |s_k>|a_k>|e_k>|o_k>, and unitary dynamics, which keeps a pure state pure, never selects one term.

title: The insolubility theorem: a mixed apparatus does not help
establishes: If a unitary coupling with an apparatus in any state rho_A = sum_j r_j |a_j><a_j|, pure or mixed, measures a projective observable with two distinct eigenvalues so that each eigenstate phi_k ends with pointer value k for certain, then for psi = (phi_1 + phi_2)/sqrt2 the final state has a block between the pointer eigenspaces Q_1 and Q_2 of squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm sum_j r_j^2/4 > 0, so it is not a mixture of states with definite pointer values (Fine 1970; Busch-Shimony 1996).
gap: Omitted: the extension to unsharp pointers and to measurements that reproduce the Born weights only approximately. Why: it needs a longer argument on the pointer's effects and nothing later uses it. Where: P. Busch, A. Shimony, Stud. Hist. Phil. Mod. Phys. 27, 397 (1996); P. Busch, P. Lahti, J.-P. Pellonpaa, K. Ylinen, Quantum Measurement (Springer 2016).
note: Certain pointer value k gives U(phi_k (x) a_j) in H (x) Q_k for each j; the (1,2) block is (1/2) sum_j r_j |U(phi_1 a_j)><U(phi_2 a_j)|, and unitarity keeps the vectors orthonormal in j.

title: The movability of the Heisenberg cut
establishes: In the von Neumann chain with orthonormal records, applying the Born rule and the Luders update to the records of link j gives the same state of the whole chain for every j up to the last completed link, because P_i^(j)Psi = P_i^(1)Psi, so no observable locates the cut among completed links; collapse anywhere differs from purely unitary evolution only for observables that do not commute with the record projectors, which are the observables that detect interference between branches.

title: The measurement problem as Maudlin's trilemma
establishes: The three claims that the wavefunction is complete, that it always evolves linearly, and that measurements have single definite outcomes are jointly inconsistent with the von Neumann chain, and each interpretation rejects at least one of them.

title: Proper and improper mixtures
establishes: A proper mixture (an ensemble prepared by chance) and an improper mixture (the reduced state of an entangled whole) can have the same density operator and so the same statistics on the system, while joint measurements with the environment distinguish them, so the formalism alone does not license reading a reduced state as ignorance of a definite state.

title: Decoherence of a qubit by N environment qubits
establishes: Under H = hbar Z (x) sum_k g_k Z_k with the environment in a product state, the qubit's populations are constant and its coherence is multiplied by the decoherence factor r(t) = prod_k (|alpha_k|^2 exp(-2i g_k t) + |beta_k|^2 exp(2i g_k t)), of modulus at most 1.

title: Decay of the decoherence factor
establishes: For |alpha_k|^2 = 1/2, |r(t)| = prod_k |cos 2 g_k t| <= exp(-2 t^2 sum_k g_k^2) while t <= pi/(4 max_k g_k), by Taylor bounds on cos and exp; at the end of that window the bound is exp(-(pi^2/8) sum_k g_k^2 / max_k g_k^2), so coherence is lost within a time of order (sum_k g_k^2)^(-1/2) when many couplings are comparable.

title: Recurrence of coherence in finite environments
establishes: For finitely many couplings g_k, |r(t)| returns arbitrarily close to 1 at arbitrarily late times, by Dirichlet's simultaneous approximation theorem proved with the pigeonhole principle, so decoherence by a finite environment is reversible in principle.

title: Pointer states and the commutation criterion
establishes: For H = A (x) B + I (x) H_E with B not a multiple of I (the system's own Hamiltonian set to zero), a pure system state remains unentangled with the environment for every environment state and every t iff it lies in one eigenspace of A; these eigenspaces define the pointer basis, and a weak system Hamiltonian perturbs it (next session).

title: A dephased, driven qubit: the Bloch equations and the slow rate
establishes: For d rho/dt = -(i omega/2)[X, rho] + (gamma/2)(Z rho Z - rho), the Bloch equations are linear: x decays at rate gamma, and the (y, z) block M = [[-gamma, -omega], [omega, 0]] has eigenvalues (-gamma +- sqrt(gamma^2 - 4 omega^2))/2, so for omega << gamma the slow rate is omega^2/gamma + O(omega^4/gamma^3).

title: Einselection: the predictability sieve
establishes: With M = S diag(l_s, l_f) S^{-1} from the previous session (l_s > l_f), exp(tM) = e^{l_s t} u v^T + e^{l_f t} u' v'^T, where v and v' are the rows of S^{-1} (the left eigenvectors), so the unit Bloch vector r maximising |exp(tM) r| at times t >> 1/gamma tends to the left slow eigenvector, to first order in omega/gamma +-(0, omega/gamma, 1)/norm near the Z eigenstates, and its |r|^2 decays at the Zeno rate 2 omega^2/gamma: the predictability sieve selects the pointer states of the previous section, perturbed by the weak Hamiltonian.
note: In the (y,z) block M = [[-gamma,-omega],[omega,0]] the slow eigenvalue is about -omega^2/gamma; its RIGHT eigenvector has y = -(omega/gamma)z, its LEFT eigenvector y = +(omega/gamma)z, and the late-time amplitude is maximised along the left one (check: gamma=1, omega=0.1, t=50 gives optimal y/z = 0.101).

title: Quantum Darwinism: redundant records
establishes: For a branching state sum_i c_i |s_i>|e_i^1>...|e_i^N> with orthonormal s_i and <e_i^k|e_j^k> = 0 for i != j and every k, every nonempty proper fragment F of the environment has I(S:F) = H(|c_i|^2) while the whole environment has twice that, so the pointer information is held N-fold redundantly.

title: Quantum Darwinism: imperfect records and experiments
establishes: With imperfect records the mutual-information plateau is approximate and redundancy is defined with an information deficit, and photonic and NV-centre experiments (Ciampini et al. 2018; Unden et al. 2019) measured such plateaus.

title: Experiment: observing decoherence
establishes: Brune et al. (1996) measured the progressive decoherence of a superposition of two field states in a microwave cavity, faster for more widely separated states, and Hornberger et al. (2003) measured the loss of C70 fringe visibility as a function of background-gas pressure; both behave as the model of decoherence-model and decoherence-timescale predicts when the couplings g_k grow with the separation of the two branches or the number of environment systems grows with the pressure, and the cavity and collisional models themselves are not derived.

title: What decoherence does not do
establishes: Decoherence makes reduced states diagonal in the pointer basis and records redundant, but the global state remains a pure superposition, the reduced state is an improper mixture, and nothing in the unitary model selects one outcome, so decoherence alone does not resolve Maudlin's trilemma.

title: Problems for Part XXIII
establishes: Integrated problems on cut placement, decoherence factors, pointer states and mutual-information plateaus, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Observers inside the system (Q2)
goal: Treat observers as quantum systems: Wigner's friend, Breuer's theorem on self-measurement, Frauchiger-Renner, Brukner's theorem and local friendliness with its experiments, relational quantum mechanics and quantum reference frames.

title: Wigner's friend
establishes: If the friend applies the state update inside a sealed lab while Wigner describes the lab unitarily, the two assign different states, and these give different statistics only for measurements whose projectors have nonzero matrix elements between the friend's record branches; for example, Wigner assigns probability 1 to the projector onto (|0>|F0> + |1>|F1>)/sqrt2, and the updated description assigns it 1/2.

title: Deutsch's version of Wigner's friend
establishes: If the friend's memory records 'I observed a definite outcome' in a register that does not depend on which outcome, Wigner can reverse the measurement, keep that record, and still observe interference, so the existence of a definite outcome for the friend becomes a statement inside unitary quantum mechanics.

title: Measurements as inference maps
establishes: A measurement of a system O by an apparatus A is an inference map theta from sets of A-states to sets of O-states with theta(S_A) = union over s_A in S_A of theta({s_A}), all states referring to the same time after the interaction; a state s_o is exactly measurable if theta(S_A) = {s_o} for some S_A, and s1, s2 are distinguishable if some S_A^1, S_A^2 have s1 in theta(S_A^1), s2 not in theta(S_A^1), s2 in theta(S_A^2) and s1 not in theta(S_A^2).
note: Follow T. Breuer, Philos. Sci. 62, 197-214 (1995), secs. 3.1-3.2.

title: Measurement from inside: proper inclusion and meshing
establishes: For O = A + R with a surjective restriction s -> s|_A (dropping coordinates classically, the partial trace in quantum mechanics), proper inclusion means that some s != s' have s|_A = s'|_A, an assumption about the restriction map rather than a cardinality count (which suffices only for finitely many states), and meshing means theta({s_A})|_A = {s_A} for every s_A: inferred O-states restrict to the apparatus's own present state.
note: Breuer 1995, secs. 3.3-3.4.

title: Breuer's theorem: no complete measurement from inside
establishes: Meshing implies theta({s_A}) = {s in theta(S_A) : s|_A = s_A}, so if s1|_A = s2|_A no meshing inference map distinguishes s1 and s2 (Prop. 2), and with proper inclusion some state of O is not exactly measurable from inside (Prop. 1); hence no measurement from inside is informationally complete, classically and quantum mechanically, for deterministic or stochastic dynamics, and exact measurability of all states would violate meshing (the Goedel analogy).
note: Breuer 1995, secs. 3.4-3.5. Prop. 1: if theta(S_A) = {s}, meshing forces S_A = {s|_A}, so theta({s|_A}) = {s} and likewise {s'} for s' != s with the same restriction, a contradiction. Prop. 2: s1 in theta(S^1) forces s_A in S^1, s2 in theta(S^2) forces s_A in S^2, and theta({s_A}) contains both s1, s2 and lies in both sets. Stress that counting arguments are not the proof.

title: Breuer's theorem and EPR correlations
establishes: Pure states sum_k sqrt(lambda_k) e^{i phi_k}|a_k>|r_k> and sum_k sqrt(lambda_k) e^{i phi'_k}|a_k>|r_k> of A (x) R with Schmidt rank at least 2 and phase differences phi_k - phi'_k not constant in k are distinct but have identical reduced states on A and on R, so by Prop. 2 an apparatus A cannot distinguish them; quantum mechanics has uncountably many pure states with the same restrictions, whereas a classical pure state (a, r) is fixed by its restrictions.
note: Breuer 1995, sec. 4.

title: What measurement from inside can still do
establishes: Measurement from inside can still distinguish states with different restrictions to A and can measure some states of O exactly, but never all, so no experiment distinguishes all states of the universe and a universally valid theory can be valid only in a relative, observer-dependent sense (Breuer 1995, sec. 5).
note: Breuer 1995, sec. 5. Optional remark or problem: a unitary on S = A (x) R followed by a projective readout of A has effects U^dagger(Q_j (x) I_R)U, whose ranks are multiples of dim R.

title: The Frauchiger-Renner setup
establishes: Two friends act on a coin prepared in sqrt(1/3)|h> + sqrt(2/3)|t> and on a spin prepared according to the coin, two Wigners measure the friends' labs in rotated bases, and the four-party state after the friends' pre-measurements is written explicitly in the bases the Wigners measure.

title: The Frauchiger-Renner chain of inferences
establishes: Using only Born-rule predictions with probability one (assumption Q), each agent derives a certain statement about another agent's outcome, and chaining these by consistency (assumption C) predicts that the joint Wigner outcome (ok, ok) never occurs.

title: The Frauchiger-Renner contradiction and its assumptions
establishes: Direct calculation gives (ok, ok) probability 1/12, so Q, C and the single-outcome assumption S cannot all hold for agents modelled as quantum systems, and the session records which assumption each response rejects.

title: Brukner's no-go theorem for observer-independent facts
establishes: In a two-lab Wigner's-friend scenario, assuming that the friends' and the Wigners' outcomes jointly have values (observer-independent facts), together with locality and free choice, implies a Bell inequality that quantum theory applied to the friends violates.

title: Local friendliness: the assumptions and the polytope
establishes: Absoluteness of observed events and local agency (Bong et al. 2020) imply that the observed behaviours of a two-lab Wigner's-friend scenario are marginals of distributions over the Wigners' and friends' outcomes obeying the linear local-agency constraints; that set is bounded and cut out by finitely many linear constraints, so it is a polytope, and its image under the linear marginal map, the convex hull of the images of its vertices, is the local-friendliness polytope, containing the local polytope and contained in the no-signalling polytope.

title: With two settings per side, local friendliness equals locality
establishes: If each Wigner has two settings, one of which reveals the friend's outcome, the distribution for the two non-revealing settings already gives a joint distribution of all four outcomes with the observed pair marginals, so the local-friendliness polytope equals the local polytope.

title: With three settings per side, local friendliness is weaker than locality
establishes: With three binary settings per side, setting 1 revealing the friend's outcome, the local-friendliness polytope is the convex hull of 96 points, in each of which the friends' outcomes (c, d) are deterministic, setting 1 returns them, and settings {2,3} carry an extreme no-signalling behaviour; it strictly contains the local polytope, since a PR box on settings {2,3} is local-friendly and gives 4 on <A2B2>+<A2B3>+<A3B2>-<A3B3> <= 2; and the genuine local-friendliness inequality of Bong et al. (2020), -<A1>-<A2>-<B1>-<B2>-<A1B1>-2<A1B2>-2<A2B1>+2<A2B2>-<A2B3>-<A3B2>-<A3B3> <= 6, holds at all 96 points, with equality at some of them, so its violation refutes local friendliness and not merely locality.
gap: Omitted: that this inequality is a facet of the local-friendliness polytope but not of the local polytope, and the full list of 932 local-friendliness facets in 9 classes. Why: they come from a computer vertex-to-facet conversion (PANDA). Where: K.-W. Bong et al., Nat. Phys. 16, 1199 (2020), Suppl. Sec. B.

title: Quantum violation of a local-friendliness inequality
establishes: With friends as qubits measured unitarily and undone by the Wigners, |Phi+> with A1 = Z (the friend's measurement), A2 = X, B1 = (Z-X)/sqrt2 and B3 = -(Z+X)/sqrt2 gives 2 sqrt2 > 2 on the CHSH inequality <A1B1>-<A1B3>-<A2B1>-<A2B3> <= 2, which is a local-friendliness inequality by lf-two-settings-local applied to the sub-scenario with settings {1,2} x {1,3}.
gap: Omitted: the quantum values of the genuine local-friendliness inequality of lf-three-settings, about 7.28 for a maximally entangled state (by direct optimisation of the correlation matrix) and the maximum about 7.345 for partially entangled qubits with Schmidt coefficients about 0.776 and 0.631. Why: they were found by see-saw numerical optimisation and certified by the NPA semidefinite hierarchy. Where: K.-W. Bong et al., Nat. Phys. 16, 1199 (2020), Suppl. Sec. C for 7.345.

title: Experiments on extended Wigner's-friend scenarios
establishes: Proietti et al. (2019) tested Brukner's inequality with six photons and Bong et al. (2020) violated local-friendliness inequalities with photon paths standing in for the friends; the session states what each measured and why a photon path is a weak stand-in for an observer, which motivates proposals with larger friends (Wiseman, Cavalcanti and Rieffel 2023).

title: Relational quantum mechanics
establishes: Rovelli's relational interpretation takes states and outcomes to be relative to a physical system, which dissolves the Wigner's-friend conflict at the price of absoluteness of observed events, and the session states its postulates, the later cross-perspective-links postulate, and the objections that remain.

title: Unitary representations of finite groups and group averaging
establishes: For a unitary representation g -> U_g of a finite group, the average (1/|G|) sum_g U_g X U_g^dagger is the Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal projection of X onto the operators that commute with every U_g.

title: Missing reference frames and group averaging
establishes: If two parties do not share a Z_N phase reference, with U_g = sum_q omega^(gq) Pi_q, each sees the other's states and operations group-averaged, which by the roots-of-unity sum deletes every block Pi_q rho Pi_q' with q != q' (a superselection rule), and a shared quantum reference system restores relational coherence.

title: Changing quantum reference frames on a ring
establishes: For particles on Z_N, describing the others relative to particle A or relative to particle B is related by an explicit unitary built from controlled shifts and the inversion |x> -> |-x> (|x_B>_B|x_C>_C -> |-x_B>_A|x_C - x_B>_C) (Giacomini, Castro-Ruiz and Brukner 2019, in finite form).

title: Superposition and entanglement depend on the quantum reference frame
establishes: A state in which B is in a superposition of positions relative to A and C is localised becomes, relative to B, a state in which A and C are entangled, so entanglement and superposition are not frame-independent properties.

title: Q2 restated: measuring a system from inside
establishes: Q2 becomes the precise statements of the movable cut, Breuer's theorem, Frauchiger-Renner, Brukner's theorem and local friendliness, and the frame dependence of states, each with its assumptions.

title: Problems for Part XXIV
