establishes: Integrated problems on Wigner's-friend probabilities, self-measurement, the local-friendliness polytope and reference-frame changes, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: Interpretations
goal: State each main interpretation by what it takes as primitive, derive what can be derived inside it (the consistency condition of histories, the urgleichung, the Deutsch-Wallace and envariance arguments, Bell-Vink equivariance, GRW amplification), and map which assumption each gives up.

title: The Copenhagen family
establishes: Bohr's complementarity, Heisenberg's cut and the von Neumann-Dirac textbook collapse are distinct positions, and the session states what each takes as primitive (classical description of the apparatus, the cut, the collapse postulate) and which claim of Maudlin's trilemma each rejects.

title: Consistent histories
establishes: A family of histories, each a time-ordered product C_h of Heisenberg-picture projectors, assigns probabilities p(h) = tr(C_h rho C_h^dagger) that are additive under every coarse-graining iff the real part of its decoherence functional D(h,h') = tr(C_h rho C_h'^dagger) vanishes for h != h'; two consistent families can have no common consistent refinement, and the rule that every inference uses a single family is how the view answers Maudlin's trilemma and Frauchiger-Renner (Griffiths, Gell-Mann-Hartle, Omnes).
note: Coarse-graining h and h' gives class operator C_h + C_h', so p(h or h') = p(h) + p(h') + 2 Re D(h,h'). Source: R. B. Griffiths, Consistent Quantum Theory (CUP 2002); locate Griffiths' published reply to Frauchiger-Renner and verify the reference before writing.

title: Dutch-book coherence implies the probability axioms
establishes: An agent who prices bets on finitely many outcomes so that no combination of bets guarantees a loss must price them by a probability distribution, and conversely, by the separating hyperplane theorem.

title: The Born rule in SIC form
establishes: If p(i) is the qubit SIC distribution of rho and r(j|i) the probability of outcome j of any measurement in state Pi_i, then that measurement's distribution is q(j) = sum_i (3p(i) - 1/2) r(j|i).

title: QBism
establishes: QBism reads the quantum state as an agent's coherent degrees of belief about the outcomes of her own actions, reads the SIC form of the Born rule (the urgleichung) as a coherence condition linking a hypothetical and an actual measurement, and answers Wigner's friend and Frauchiger-Renner by denying that one agent's state assignment binds another.

title: Everett's relative states
establishes: For a global pure state of S (x) O and an observer state o_k, the relative state of S is the normalised (I (x) <o_k|) psi, and after a pre-measurement the Schmidt form writes the global state as a superposition of record branches without a collapse postulate.

title: Branching from decoherence
establishes: With redundant environmental records, an operation on S and on a set of environment fragments that leaves out a fragment holding a perfect record leaves the interference between two branches exactly zero; if the untouched fragments hold imperfect records, the interference that can be restored is bounded by the product of their overlaps |<e_i^j|e_k^j>|, so recombining branches requires acting on every fragment that carries a record.

title: The probability problem in Everett's theory
establishes: Because every outcome occurs in some branch, Born probabilities need a separate justification, either as rational credences (decision theory) or as consequences of a symmetry (envariance), and each route rests on stated assumptions.

title: Fine-graining a branch into equal-amplitude branches
establishes: For sum_k c_k|s_k>|e_k> with orthonormal e_k and |c_k|^2 = m_k/n, a unitary on E (x) ancilla alone, controlled by the records e_k, maps it to sum_k sum_{j<=m_k} n^(-1/2)|s_k>|e_k>|a_kj> with orthonormal a_kj, leaving rho_S unchanged.

title: The Deutsch-Wallace argument I: equal amplitudes
establishes: If an agent values each bet on a branching measurement by sum_k w_k u(k) with weights w_k depending only on the post-measurement state, and is indifferent to branch relabelling (axioms stated in the session), branches of equal amplitude get equal weights, because the swap exchanging them is undone by a swap on the environment.

title: The Deutsch-Wallace argument II: the Born weights
establishes: Fine-graining a branch into equal-amplitude sub-branches gives it weight |c|^2 whenever |c|^2 is rational, and a continuity axiom extends this to every amplitude.

title: Zurek's envariance argument
establishes: A unitary on S that can be undone by a unitary on an entangled environment E cannot change local probabilities, which under Zurek's assumptions forces equal probabilities for equal Schmidt coefficients and, by fine-graining, probabilities |c_k|^2 for rational squared amplitudes.

title: Objections to the Everett interpretation
establishes: The preferred-basis problem is answered by decoherence, and the remaining objections ask whether decision-theoretic weights are probabilities and whether the derivations assume what they derive; the session states each with its main reply.

title: The probability current in a finite basis
establishes: For psi(t) solving the Schrodinger equation, d|psi_i|^2/dt = sum_j J_ij with the antisymmetric current J_ij = (2/hbar) Im(conj(psi_i) H_ij psi_j).

title: Pilot-wave theory on a finite configuration space: the Bell-Vink process
establishes: Fixing a configuration basis, the rates T_{i<-j} = max(0, J_ij)/|psi_j|^2 define a master equation for the distribution of the actual configuration, guided by psi.

title: Equivariance of the Bell-Vink process
establishes: The distribution |psi_i(t)|^2 satisfies the master equation of the Bell-Vink rates, so by uniqueness, on every time interval where all |psi_j| stay away from 0, a configuration distributed as |psi|^2 at one time is so distributed at every later time.
gap: Omitted: the behaviour at times where some |psi_j|^2 vanishes, where the rates are unbounded and the uniqueness argument does not apply, and the construction of the jump process itself. Why: it needs the theory of jump processes with time-dependent unbounded rates. Where: J. C. Vink, Phys. Rev. A 48, 1808 (1993); H.-O. Georgii, R. Tumulka, Markov Process. Relat. Fields 11, 1-18 (2005).

title: Measurement in pilot-wave theory
establishes: When a pre-measurement correlates system and pointer configurations, the actual pointer configuration selects one branch, the conditional wavefunction of the system becomes the corresponding eigenstate, and the outcome frequencies are the Born probabilities by equivariance.
gap: Omitted: equivariance through times at which some |psi_j|^2 vanishes, which a pre-measurement from a sharp pointer configuration passes through. Why and where: as in bell-vink-equivariance (Vink 1993; Georgii-Tumulka 2005).

title: Nonlocality and contextuality in pilot-wave theory
establishes: In the Bell-Vink model the values of non-configuration observables depend on the measurement arrangement, consistent with Kochen-Specker, and the rates for one subsystem depend on distant settings through psi, so the model violates parameter independence for configurations while keeping no-signalling for |psi|^2-distributed ones, consistent with Bell.

title: Excursion: continuous Bohmian mechanics
establishes: On wavefunctions on R^n the guidance equation dX/dt = (hbar/m) Im(grad psi/psi)(X) and the continuity equation for |psi|^2 give equivariance formally, as the continuum counterpart of the Bell-Vink result.
gap: Omitted: partial derivatives and the Schrodinger equation i hbar d psi/dt = -(hbar^2/2m) Laplacian psi + V psi on R^n, used formally here; global existence and uniqueness of Bohmian trajectories for almost every initial configuration; the rigorous form of equivariance. Why: they need partial differential equations and measure theory. Where: K. Berndl, D. Durr, S. Goldstein, G. Peruzzi, N. Zanghi, Commun. Math. Phys. 173, 647 (1995); S. Teufel, R. Tumulka, Commun. Math. Phys. 258, 349 (2005); D. Durr, S. Teufel, Bohmian Mechanics (Springer 2009), Ch. 8.

title: A finite-dimensional GRW-type collapse model
establishes: Localisation channels applied at the times of a Poisson process of rate lambda per constituent give, on average, the master equation d rho/dt = -(i/hbar)[H,rho] + lambda sum_k (Phi_k(rho) - rho), which damps coherence between distant pointer positions.

title: Amplification in collapse models
establishes: For a pointer of K constituents in a superposition of two well-separated positions, the coherence decays at rate K lambda, so single constituents almost never collapse while macroscopic superpositions collapse within an explicit short time.

title: Excursion: continuum collapse models and experimental bounds
establishes: The continuum GRW and CSL models fix a rate lambda (about 10^-16 per second per nucleon in GRW's choice) and a length r_C (about 10^-7 m), and matter-wave interferometry, spontaneous X-ray emission from germanium, cantilever heating and gravitational-wave test masses each exclude a stated region of the (lambda, r_C) plane.
gap: Omitted: the continuum definitions of GRW and CSL and the derivation of each experimental bound. Why: they need wavefunctions on R^3 and noise models of each experiment. Where: A. Bassi, K. Lochan, S. Satin, T. P. Singh, H. Ulbricht, Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 471 (2013); M. Carlesso et al., Nat. Phys. 18, 243 (2022).

title: Which assumption each view gives up
establishes: Tabulating each interpretation, and the collapse models as rival theories, against Maudlin's three claims, Bell's assumptions (local causality, measurement independence, single outcomes), Kochen-Specker noncontextuality, PBR's preparation independence, the Frauchiger-Renner assumptions and local friendliness shows exactly which assumption each gives up.

title: Problems for Part XXV
establishes: Integrated problems on relative states, Bell-Vink rates for small systems and GRW-type master equations, which nothing later depends on, with solutions in the solutions volume.

title: The reader's own question
goal: Turn an informal question into a formal one, classify claims, judge novelty, read and write to the literature, and choose what to study next.

title: Restating an intuition inside the formalism
establishes: An informal claim becomes testable once each term is replaced by a defined object of the book (state, instrument, ontological model, behaviour, assumption), and the session does this for Q1, Q2 and Q3 in the ordinary words of Session 1.

title: Telling a theorem from a postulate or an interpretation
establishes: A claim is a theorem if it follows from stated assumptions by proof, a postulate if it is one of them, an experimental result if it reports a measured quantity with its uncertainty, and an interpretation if it adds no prediction that differs from the formalism's, so collapse models, which do differ, are rival theories rather than interpretations, with examples from every Part.

title: What would count as new
establishes: A result is new if it weakens an assumption of a known no-go theorem, gives a tighter or more general bound, proposes an experiment that separates two views, or proves an equivalence, and each is checked by reducing it to the book's assumption lists (Bell, Kochen-Specker, PBR, Breuer, local friendliness) and searching the literature under the corresponding names.

title: How to read a quant-ph paper and write to its author
establishes: A foundations paper is read by locating its scenario, its assumptions, its main inequality or theorem and its proof route, and by reproducing its smallest example, which the session does for one paper from Parts XX-XXIV; a useful message to its author then states one precise question in the paper's own notation, shows the reader's own derivation up to that step, and cites the equation it concerns.

title: Where to go next
establishes: For each Part the session names the references that continue it (infinite dimensions, quantum information theory, open systems and filtering, foundations), together with the labelled gaps of this book that each one fills.
